name: Nationwide general strike against economic reforms (NPMO / Left trade unions)
city_or_district: Multiple (strongest in West Bengal, Kerala, Tripura, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu)
trigger: Vajpayee government's privatisation of PSUs, opening of the economy and cuts in foodgrain/fertiliser subsidies
organisers: National Platform of Mass Organisations (NPMO); CITU, AITUC and other Left-affiliated trade unions
demands: Halt privatisation/disinvestment, reverse subsidy cuts, protect labour rights
state_response: Preventive arrest of about 2,000 activists in Andhra Pradesh; hundreds detained in Tamil Nadu for blocking road and rail traffic; sporadic violence in Andhra Pradesh
outcome: One-day disruption of rail, road and air traffic, factories and banks; no policy reversal
sources: https://www.tribuneindia.com/2000/20000512/main2.htm | https://labourreview.org/history-of-strikes-in-india/ (background on the series of central trade union general strikes)

name: Irom Sharmila hunger strike against AFSPA after the Malom massacre
trigger: Assam Rifles personnel shot dead 10 civilians at a bus stop in Malom on 2 Nov 2000 after an attack on their convoy
organisers: Irom Chanu Sharmila (individual fast); later backed by Meira Paibi groups and Manipur civil society
demands: Repeal of the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act 1958
state_response: Repeated arrest under IPC s.309 (attempt to suicide) and force-feeding by nasal tube in judicial custody
outcome: Fast lasted 16 years and ended 9 Aug 2016 (end date is outside catalogue window); AFSPA not repealed
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malom_Massacre | https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/why-indias-iron-lady-went-on-a-hunger-strike-for-16-years-180960075/ | https://www.tribuneindia.com/2005/20050313/society.htm | https://www.deccanherald.com/opinion/irom-woman-activist-2080235 (sources differ on fast start: 4 or 5 Nov 2000)

name: Great June Uprising against extension of NSCN-IM ceasefire to Manipur
trigger: 14 June 2001 Bangkok agreement extending the Centre-NSCN(IM) ceasefire 'without territorial limits', seen as a threat to Manipur's territorial integrity
organisers: Civil society, student and women's organisations of the Imphal valley
demands: Withdraw the territorial extension of the ceasefire; protect Manipur's territorial integrity
deaths: 18 (SATP records 13 killed on 18 June 2001; 18 are recognised as martyrs in later commemorations)
state_response: Security forces opened fire on protesters; curfew imposed; protesters burnt the State Assembly building
outcome: Union government on 27 July 2001 withdrew the 'without territorial limits' clause and reverted to original ceasefire ground rules

name: 2002 Gujarat communal violence after Godhra train burning (VHP bandh and riots) and aftermath
city_or_district: Godhra, Ahmedabad, Vadodara and other districts
trigger: Burning of coach S-6 of the Sabarmati Express at Godhra on 27 Feb 2002 killing 58 karsevaks returning from Ayodhya
organisers: Vishwa Hindu Parishad called a statewide bandh on 28 Feb 2002 (HRW documents support from state BJP); mobs
demands: n/a (bandh called in protest at Godhra; violence was retaliatory)
deaths: 1044 (official: 790 Muslims and 254 Hindus; 223 missing; unofficial estimates up to 2,000)
state_response: Delayed army deployment; HRW documented police inaction and complicity; Nanavati-Shah Commission and later SC-appointed SIT
outcome: Violence in Ahmedabad continued about three months; mass displacement into relief camps; decade of prosecutions; civil-society and victims' protests followed (end date approximate: main phase)
election_within_6_months: no (Gujarat assembly election 2002-12-12 was about 9 months after onset)

name: VHP Ram temple 'shila daan' agitation at Ayodhya
trigger: VHP deadline to begin Ram temple construction on 15 March 2002; Supreme Court order of 13 March 2002 barring any religious activity on the acquired land
organisers: Vishwa Hindu Parishad; Ram Janmabhoomi Nyas
demands: Hand over undisputed acquired land to the Nyas and begin temple construction
crowd_press: hundreds of volunteers reported in Ayodhya
state_response: Supreme Court status-quo order of 13 March 2002; heavy security deployment in Ayodhya
outcome: Ceremony reduced to a symbolic stone offering; no construction began
election_within_6_months: yes: Uttar Pradesh assembly election Feb 2002 (concluded weeks before)

name: Nationwide general strike of central trade unions
trigger: Trade union sponsoring committee call against NDA government's privatisation/disinvestment and proposed labour-law changes
organisers: HMS, AITUC, CITU and other Left-leaning central trade unions (INTUC did not join)
demands: Halt disinvestment and labour-law amendments; protect public sector jobs
state_response: No reported action; normal life at standstill in Ludhiana and Left-ruled states per Tribune
outcome: One-day strike; no policy change

name: Cauvery water-release agitation in Karnataka
trigger: Supreme Court / Cauvery River Authority orders directing drought-hit Karnataka to release water to Tamil Nadu; CM S.M. Krishna's defiance
organisers: Cauvery-basin farmers' organisations, pro-Kannada outfits and political parties (rallies and padyatras)
demands: No release of Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu until Karnataka's own needs are met
state_response: Karnataka government initially defied the SC order; SC on 24 Oct 2002 indicted the state for wilful disobedience
outcome: Karnataka released water after the SC rebuke; dispute continued to the 2007 tribunal award (start date set to first of month: only month known)

name: Dulina (Jhajjar) Dalit lynching and Dalit protests
trigger: Mob of over 1,000 lynched five Dalit men who were skinning a dead cow outside Dulina police post on 15 Oct 2002
organisers: Dalit organisations and parties protesting in Haryana and Delhi; VHP leaders publicly defended the mob
demands: Arrest and prosecution of the lynch mob; compensation; action against police who failed to protect the men
crowd_press: mob of over 1,000 (press/academic accounts of the lynching)
state_response: CM O.P. Chautala announced Rs 1 lakh compensation per family; 23 arrested by 2 Dec 2002, 10 more wanted
outcome: Prosecutions proceeded; case became a reference point for cow-protection lynchings (end date approximate)

name: Muthanga adivasi land occupation and police firing
trigger: State's failure to honour Oct 2001 agreement to allot land to landless adivasis; AGMS occupation of about 5,000 acres inside the sanctuary from 4 Jan 2003
organisers: Adivasi Gothra Maha Sabha (C.K. Janu, M. Geethanandan)
demands: Allotment of promised land to landless adivasi families
crowd_press: hundreds of adivasi families occupying the land
deaths: 2 (adivasi protester Jogi and police constable Vinod; some accounts give an official toll of 5)
state_response: Eviction operation by Kerala Police and Forest Department on 19 Feb 2003; 18 rounds fired; huts torched; leaders arrested
outcome: Occupation ended; land distribution to adivasis still incomplete two decades later

name: Tamil Nadu government employees' and teachers' indefinite strike and mass dismissals
trigger: AIADMK government's unilateral cuts to pensions and other benefits of state employees
organisers: State government employees' and teachers' associations
demands: Restoration of pensions and withdrawn benefits
crowd_press: about 200,000 strikers (WSWS); ITUC records 350,000 employees dismissed
state_response: Mass dismissal of striking employees under state essential-services law; Supreme Court in T.K. Rangarajan v. Govt of Tamil Nadu (Aug 2003) upheld the state and held government employees have no fundamental right to strike
outcome: Strike collapsed; SC ruling became the trigger for the 24 Feb 2004 nationwide strike (dates set to month: exact start/end not in sources found)

name: Nationwide general strike against Supreme Court ruling denying the right to strike
city_or_district: Multiple (West Bengal, Bengaluru and Mumbai worst hit)
trigger: Supreme Court T.K. Rangarajan judgment (Aug 2003) that public employees have no right to strike; disinvestment and pension policy
organisers: Central trade unions and central/state government employees' federations, public-sector bank unions
demands: Statutory protection of the right to strike; halt privatisation; defend pensions
crowd_press: more than 10 million (VOA / WSWS)
state_response: Strike went ahead in defiance of court ruling; no major repression reported
outcome: One-day shutdown of government offices, state-owned banks, schools and public transport in most major cities
election_within_6_months: yes: Lok Sabha general election 2004-04-20 to 2004-05-10

name: Thangjam Manorama killing protests and Meira Paibi nude protest against AFSPA
trigger: Thangjam Manorama (32) taken from her home by 17 Assam Rifles on 10 July 2004 and found dead on 11 July; investigations recorded torture and rape
organisers: Meira Paibi women's groups; Apunba Lup (coalition of 32 organisations); student bodies
demands: Repeal of AFSPA; prosecution of Assam Rifles personnel responsible
crowd_press: 12 Meira Paibi women staged the nude protest at Kangla Fort on 15 July 2004; wider agitation crowd figures not published
state_response: Curfew, arrests and lathicharge; Union government withdrew AFSPA from Imphal municipal area and appointed the Justice Jeevan Reddy committee (HRW)
outcome: AFSPA lifted from Imphal municipal area (Aug 2004); Reddy committee recommended repeal in 2005 but was not acted on; no prosecutions (end date approximate)

name: Honda Motorcycle and Scooter India workers' protest and police lathicharge, Gurgaon
trigger: Suspension of 50 and dismissal of 4 HMSI workers (May 2005) over union organising, following a wage dispute since Dec 2004; lockout
organisers: HMSI workers with AITUC/CITU support; workers from neighbouring factories and families joined
demands: Reinstatement of suspended/dismissed workers; recognition of union; wage revision
crowd_press: 2,000-3,000 workers (libcom account)
state_response: Haryana Police lathicharge and tear gas at the mini-secretariat; about 60-70 workers seriously injured; Justice G.C. Garg inquiry commission appointed
outcome: Televised police violence caused national outrage; settlement reinstating workers followed; Garg Commission report submitted Jan 2006

name: Nationwide general strike of central trade unions (16-point charter)
city_or_district: Delhi, Kerala, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Punjab (major centres)
trigger: UPA government's disinvestment, price rise, labour-law violations and outsourcing
organisers: Sponsoring Committee of Trade Unions (all central trade unions except INTUC)
demands: 16-point charter: halt privatisation, enforce labour laws, curb price rise, social security for unorganised workers
crowd_organiser: over 60 million (union claim reported by Labour File)
state_response: No major repression reported in sources
outcome: One-day disruption of airlines, banks, insurance, roadways, coal, postal, telecom, defence units and petroleum sector

name: Kalinganagar police firing on adivasi protesters against Tata Steel plant
trigger: Construction of a boundary wall for Tata Steel's plant on land acquired from adivasi villagers without agreed resettlement
organisers: Local adivasi villagers organised under the anti-displacement platform (Visthapan Virodhi Jan Manch)
demands: Stop land acquisition and boundary wall; fair compensation and rehabilitation
deaths: 14 (13 adivasis including three women and a 12-year-old boy, plus one policeman; Amnesty records 12 adivasis)
state_response: Police firing on protesters; official inquiry; no one held accountable
outcome: Adivasis blockaded the highway for over a year; plant eventually built; rehabilitation and land titles unresolved years later

name: Narmada Bachao Andolan Delhi dharna and Medha Patkar's 20-day fast against raising Sardar Sarovar dam
state: Madhya Pradesh / Gujarat / Maharashtra (protest held in Delhi)
trigger: Narmada Control Authority's 8 March 2006 approval to raise Sardar Sarovar dam height to 121.92 m before rehabilitation of oustees
organisers: Narmada Bachao Andolan (Medha Patkar)
demands: Halt dam-raising until all displaced families are rehabilitated with land
state_response: Police removed Patkar to hospital on the 8th day of her fast; Supreme Court heard NBA petition but declined to stop construction immediately
outcome: Fast ended 17 Apr 2006 after SC said it would stop construction if rehabilitation found inadequate by 1 May 2006; dam-raising continued (31-day sit-in at Jantar Mantar)

name: Anti-OBC-quota protests by medical students and doctors (Youth for Equality)
state: Delhi (national; also Maharashtra, Punjab/Chandigarh and other states)
trigger: HRD Minister Arjun Singh's April 2006 announcement of 27% OBC reservation in central higher-education institutions (IITs, IIMs, AIIMS)
organisers: Youth for Equality; AIIMS Resident Doctors' Association and Faculty Association; medical students across cities
demands: Roll back the 27% OBC quota; white paper on reservation; alternative affirmative action
crowd_press: nearly 100,000 at Delhi rally on 27 May 2006 (nvdatabase); 28 medical students lathicharged in Mumbai on 13 May
state_response: Police lathicharge on students in Mumbai; government refused rollback; courts directed striking doctors back to work
outcome: Strike phase ended early June 2006; quota legislated and upheld by Supreme Court (10 Apr 2008), which ended the protest campaign (end date approximate: main strike phase)

name: Singur land acquisition protests against Tata Nano plant
trigger: Acquisition of 997 acres of farmland for Tata Motors small-car plant (announced May 2006; Mamata Banerjee fast began 2006-12-03; indefinite dharna at Singur from 2008-08-24)
organisers: Trinamool Congress (Mamata Banerjee), Krishi Jami Raksha Committee, unwilling farmers
demands: Return of 400 acres to unwilling farmers; adequate compensation
crowd_press: thousands at Aug 2008 dharna (press)
state_response: Left Front government defended acquisition; police deployed at site; talks mediated by Governor Aug-Sept 2008
outcome: Tata Motors announced withdrawal from Singur 2008-10-03 and relocated plant to Sanand, Gujarat
election_within_6_months: yes (Lok Sabha Apr-May 2009; start date approximate - acquisition notification mid-2006, day not in sources)

name: Khairlanji massacre protests and Kanpur Ambedkar-statue riots
city_or_district: Bhandara, Nagpur, Mumbai and other cities
trigger: Lynching of four members of Dalit Bhotmange family at Khairlanji on 2006-09-29 and alleged police cover-up; desecration of Ambedkar statue in Kanpur on 2006-11-28
organisers: Dalit organisations, Ambedkarite groups, Republican Party factions (largely spontaneous)
demands: Arrest and prosecution of killers; CBI probe; action against police
state_response: Police action against rioters; case transferred to CBI; fast-track trial (6 convicted 2008; death sentences commuted 2010)
outcome: Convictions in 2008; Bombay HC commuted death sentences to life 2010
election_within_6_months: no (start date is first of month - protests began first week of Nov 2006)

name: Nationwide general strike of central trade unions
trigger: Sponsoring Committee of Trade Unions call against UPA government's privatisation, disinvestment and labour-law violations
organisers: Left-aligned central trade unions (CITU, AITUC, HMS, AIUTUC, UTUC and others)
demands: Stop privatisation and disinvestment; price control; enforce labour laws; social security for unorganised workers
state_response: No special action reported; West Bengal and Kerala shut down, Delhi rally
outcome: One-day strike; no policy change

name: Nandigram anti-SEZ land protests and police firing
trigger: Haldia Development Authority notice (Jan 2007) for acquiring land for Salim Group chemical hub SEZ; police operation of 2007-03-14
organisers: Bhumi Uchhed Pratirodh Committee (Trinamool Congress, Congress, SUCI, Jamiat Ulema-e-Hind and others)
demands: Withdrawal of chemical hub/SEZ land acquisition
crowd_press: ~5,000 villagers at entry points on 2007-03-14 (Wikipedia-derived; unverified in news source)
state_response: 3,000-strong police operation 2007-03-14; Calcutta HC ordered CBI probe 2007-03-15; CPI(M) 'recapture' of Nandigram Nov 2007; CRPF deployed
outcome: Chemical hub shelved; agitation lasted ~18 months and contributed to Left Front defeat in 2011
election_within_6_months: yes (panchayat polls May 2008; start date approximate - notice issued early Jan 2007)

name: Dera Sacha Sauda-Sikh clashes
trigger: Newspaper advertisement (2007-05-13) showing Dera chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh dressed in attire resembling Guru Gobind Singh
organisers: Sikh organisations (SGPC, Akal Takht jathedars, Damdami Taksal and others) vs Dera followers
demands: Apology from Dera chief; closure of Dera branches in Punjab
crowd_press: tens of thousands of Sikhs on streets (press)
state_response: Curfew in Bathinda; heavy police deployment; FIR against Dera chief
outcome: Akal Takht edict ordering Dera premises in Punjab closed by 2007-05-27; Dera issued qualified apology

name: Gujjar Scheduled Tribe reservation agitation 2007
city_or_district: Dausa (Patoli, Sikandra), Bundi, Karauli, Bharatpur, Sawai Madhopur
trigger: State government refusal to recommend ST status for Gujjars (promised by BJP in 2003 campaign)
organisers: Gujjar Arakshan Sangharsh Samiti (Col Kirori Singh Bainsla)
demands: Reclassification of Gujjars from OBC to Scheduled Tribe
deaths: 27 (The Wire; other reports range 26-28 incl. at least 1 policeman)
state_response: Police firing at Patoli (2007-05-29) and Bundi/Sikandra; army deployed; Chopra committee set up
outcome: Agitation suspended after talks; Chopra committee report Dec 2007 rejected ST demand, leading to 2008 agitation
election_within_6_months: no (Rajasthan assembly Dec 2008; end date approximate)

name: Gorkhaland agitation (Gorkha Janmukti Morcha)
trigger: Launch of GJM by Bimal Gurung after split from Subhash Ghisingh's GNLF; Sixth Schedule proposal rejected by hill people
organisers: Gorkha Janmukti Morcha (Bimal Gurung)
demands: Separate state of Gorkhaland
state_response: Repeated bandhs met with police deployment; tripartite talks from 2008; CBI probe into Madan Tamang murder (2010-05-21)
outcome: Tripartite GTA agreement signed 2011-07-18; GTA bill passed 2011-09-02

name: Kolkata violence over Nandigram and Taslima Nasreen
trigger: Protest against CPI(M) violence in Nandigram and continued stay of Bangladeshi writer Taslima Nasreen
organisers: All India Minority Forum (Idris Ali) and allied groups
demands: Expulsion of Taslima Nasreen; action over Nandigram
state_response: Army deployed in Kolkata on afternoon of 2007-11-21; curfew in affected areas
outcome: Taslima Nasreen moved out of Kolkata to Rajasthan and then Delhi

name: MNS agitation against north Indian migrants
city_or_district: Mumbai, Pune, Nashik, Aurangabad and other cities
trigger: MNS-Samajwadi Party clash at Dadar (2008-02-03) and Raj Thackeray's remarks on north Indian migrants and Chhath Puja
organisers: Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (Raj Thackeray)
demands: Priority for Marathi speakers; end to north Indian 'display of strength'
state_response: Raj Thackeray and Abu Azmi arrested 2008-02-13; preventive detentions of MNS workers
outcome: Attacks subsided; ~25,000 north Indian workers reported fled Pune and 15,000 Nashik
election_within_6_months: no (end date approximate - attacks tapered through Feb 2008)

name: Gujjar reservation agitation 2008
trigger: Chopra committee's rejection of ST status; renewed rail/road blockade led by Col Bainsla
organisers: Gujjar Arakshan Sangharsh Samiti (Col Kirori Singh Bainsla)
demands: Scheduled Tribe status / 5 per cent separate quota
state_response: Police firing at Bayana (2008-05-23) and Sikandra (2008-05-24); army on standby; talks with CM Vasundhara Raje
outcome: Agreement on 5 per cent special backward class quota; Rajasthan assembly passed reservation bill (Gujjars, Gadia Luhars, Rebaris, Banjaras)

name: Amarnath shrine land transfer row (Jammu and Kashmir agitations)
trigger: Allotment of 40 ha forest land at Baltal to Shri Amarnath Shrine Board (order 2008-05-26); Kashmir protests forced cancellation 2008-07-01, triggering Jammu counter-agitation
organisers: Kashmir: Hurriyat and Action Committee Against Land Transfer; Jammu: Shri Amarnath Yatra Sangharsh Samiti (BJP, VHP, Bajrang Dal, Congress dissidents)
demands: Kashmir: revoke land transfer; Jammu: restore land to Shrine Board
deaths: n/a (at least 1 killed by army firing at Kathua 2008-08-06; several others reported)
state_response: Curfew in Jammu and Kashmir regions; army deployed; PDP withdrew from government and CM Azad resigned 2008-07-07; Governor's rule
outcome: Agreement 2008-08-31 giving Shrine Board exclusive use of Baltal land during yatra; Jammu agitation called off

name: Kashmir 2008 unrest (economic blockade and Muzaffarabad march)
trigger: Alleged economic blockade of Kashmir Valley by Jammu agitators; killing of Hurriyat leader Sheikh Abdul Aziz at Uri during Muzaffarabad Chalo march 2008-08-11
organisers: Hurriyat Conference factions, Coordination Committee (Muzaffarabad Chalo, Pampore Chalo, Eidgah Chalo, Lal Chowk Chalo calls)
demands: Opening of Srinagar-Muzaffarabad road for trade; azadi/self-determination
crowd_press: hundreds of thousands at Eidgah/Pampore rallies (press; estimates vary)
deaths: 72 civilians (separatist data); 5 killed at Uri 2008-08-11 incl. Sheikh Abdul Aziz
state_response: Curfew across valley; firing on marches; Lal Chowk Chalo (2008-08-24) suppressed
outcome: Cross-LoC trade opened Oct 2008; assembly elections held Nov-Dec 2008 with high turnout
election_within_6_months: yes (J&K assembly Nov-Dec 2008; end date approximate)

name: Nationwide general strike of central trade unions
trigger: Price rise and UPA government's economic/labour policies; bank mergers and outsourcing
organisers: Sponsoring Committee of Trade Unions (CITU, AITUC, HMS, AICCTU, AIUTUC, UTUC) and bank, insurance, telecom federations
demands: Curb price rise; stop privatisation and bank mergers; enforce labour laws; social security for unorganised workers
state_response: No special action reported; West Bengal, Kerala, Tripura shut down; ~40,000 bank branches affected
outcome: One-day strike; no policy change

name: Kandhamal anti-Christian violence
trigger: Murder of VHP leader Swami Laxmanananda Saraswati and four others at Jalespata ashram on 2008-08-23
organisers: VHP, Bajrang Dal and allied Hindutva groups (mobs)
demands: Retaliation for Swami's murder; opposition to conversions
state_response: Curfew; CRPF deployment; relief camps for ~54,000 displaced; judicial commission; later convictions in Swami murder case
outcome: Violence subsided by late 2008; thousands remained displaced; convictions of 7 in Swami murder case 2013
election_within_6_months: yes (Lok Sabha and Odisha assembly Apr 2009; end date approximate)

name: Lalgarh adivasi movement (PCPA)
trigger: Police raids and alleged atrocities on adivasi villagers after landmine attack on CM Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's convoy at Salboni on 2008-11-02
organisers: Police Santrash Birodhi Janasadharaner Committee / PCPA (Chhatradhar Mahato); CPI (Maoist) involvement
demands: Public apology by police; withdrawal of police camps; end to atrocities; development
state_response: Area blockaded by villagers for months; joint central-state forces operation launched June 2009 ('Operation Lalgarh'); Chhatradhar Mahato arrested Sept 2009
outcome: State regained control of Lalgarh by late June 2009; Maoist-state conflict continued to 2011
election_within_6_months: yes (Lok Sabha Apr-May 2009; end date approximate)

name: Telangana statehood movement: KCR fast-unto-death phase
trigger: K Chandrashekar Rao's fast-unto-death for separate Telangana launched at Alganoor near Siddipet 2009-11-29
organisers: Telangana Rashtra Samithi (KCR); Osmania University students; employee unions
demands: Separate Telangana state
state_response: KCR arrested and hospitalised; police action on Osmania University campus; Union Home Minister Chidambaram statement 2009-12-09
outcome: Centre announced 2009-12-09 that process of forming Telangana would be initiated; KCR ended fast; Seemandhra backlash followed

name: Kashmir 2010 unrest (stone-pelting protests)
trigger: Death of 17-year-old Tufail Mattoo hit by police teargas shell near Gani Memorial Stadium, Srinagar, 2010-06-11; earlier Machil fake-encounter killings
organisers: Largely spontaneous youth protests; Hurriyat (G) 'Quit Kashmir' protest calendars (Syed Ali Shah Geelani)
demands: Justice for killings; withdrawal of troops; azadi
state_response: Prolonged curfews; CRPF/police firing; all-party delegation Sept 2010; Centre's eight-point plan and interlocutors
outcome: Protests tapered by Oct 2010; interlocutors appointed; no prosecutions in Mattoo case

name: Bharat bandh against fuel price hike (NDA and Left)
trigger: Petrol price decontrol and hike in petrol, diesel, kerosene and LPG prices (June 2010)
organisers: BJP-led NDA (Nitin Gadkari, Sharad Yadav), Left parties, TDP, SP, JD(S), INLD, PMK
demands: Rollback of fuel price hike
state_response: Opposition leaders (Gadkari, Rajnath Singh, Jaitley, Sharad Yadav) courted arrest in Delhi and Lucknow
outcome: No rollback; FICCI estimated GDP loss ~Rs 13,000 crore (Assocham Rs 10,000 crore, CII Rs 3,000 crore)

name: Tappal (Aligarh) farmers' protest against Yamuna Expressway land acquisition
trigger: Low compensation for land acquired for Yamuna Expressway; arrest of farmer leader Rambabu Katheliya on eve of Independence Day
organisers: Local farmers (Katheliya-led committee); later Rahul Gandhi/Congress and other parties
demands: Higher compensation on par with Noida rates; release of leaders
state_response: Police firing at Jikarpur 2010-08-14; Rahul Gandhi detained entering area
outcome: UP government revised compensation policy (Sept 2010); protests continued in Mathura and Noida belt

name: Nationwide general strike of central trade unions
trigger: Price rise, disinvestment, contractualisation and non-enforcement of labour laws
organisers: Coordination Committee of Central Trade Unions (INTUC, AITUC, HMS, CITU, AIUTUC, TUCC, AICCTU, UTUC and others; BMS did not join)
demands: Curb price rise; stop disinvestment; enforce labour laws; universal social security; end contract labour in permanent jobs
state_response: No special action reported; banking, coal, port, transport sectors hit
outcome: One-day strike; no policy change

name: Jat reservation agitation (rail blockades), Haryana
trigger: Demand for OBC quota for Jats; police firing killing Sunil Sheoran at Mayyar during Sept 2010 blockade; agitation resumed March 2011
organisers: All India Jat Arakshan Sangharsh Samiti (Hawa Singh Sangwan, later Yashpal Malik)
demands: Inclusion of Jats in central OBC list; compensation and job for family of Sunil Sheoran
state_response: Police firing Sept 2010; rail traffic suspended for days; CM talks with Samiti
outcome: Blockade lifted after CM intervention; Haryana included Jats in state special backward class list 2012-2013
election_within_6_months: no (end date approximate - first of month convention not used; March 2011 phase end day not in sources)

name: Anti-POSCO land protests, Jagatsinghpur (2011-13 phase)
trigger: Odisha government's push (2011) to acquire land and demolish betel vines for POSCO steel plant; road blockade from 2011-01-26; lathi charge 2011-05-15; bomb blast at Patana 2013-03-02
organisers: POSCO Pratirodh Sangram Samiti (Abhay Sahoo)
demands: Withdrawal of POSCO project; no land acquisition; release of arrested activists
state_response: Police lathi charge and arrests 2011; betel vine demolitions; Abhay Sahoo arrested 2013
outcome: Land acquisition partly completed 2013; POSCO formally withdrew 2017; movement began 2005 but earlier phase not sourced here

name: Telangana Million March
trigger: Srikrishna Committee report (Dec 2010) and Centre's delay on Telangana; TJAC call for 'Million March' to Tank Bund
organisers: Telangana Joint Action Committee (Prof Kodandaram), TRS, BJP, Telangana MLAs
demands: Immediate introduction of Telangana statehood bill
crowd_press: thousands (press)
state_response: Police denied permission, detained MLAs and leaders, lathi charge; later cases against TRS leaders (acquitted 2024)
outcome: Statues of Telugu icons on Tank Bund vandalised; movement intensified

name: Anna Hazare Jantar Mantar fast for Jan Lokpal Bill
trigger: 2G, CWG and other scams; government's refusal to include civil society in drafting Lokpal Bill
organisers: India Against Corruption (Anna Hazare, Arvind Kejriwal, Kiran Bedi, Prashant Bhushan)
demands: Joint drafting committee for a Jan Lokpal Bill
state_response: Government accepted demand 2011-04-08; gazette notification of joint drafting committee (5 government + 5 civil society)
outcome: Fast ended 2011-04-09 after notification
election_within_6_months: yes (assembly elections in WB, TN, Kerala, Assam Apr-May 2011)

name: Jaitapur nuclear plant protest and police firing
trigger: Proposed 9,900 MW Areva-NPCIL nuclear park; Fukushima accident (March 2011) heightened fears; land acquisition and fishing livelihood concerns
organisers: Konkan Bachao Samiti, Janhit Seva Samiti, local fishermen; Shiv Sena supported
demands: Scrapping of Jaitapur nuclear project
state_response: Police firing at Sakhri Nate; entry of anti-nuclear activists barred; bandh in Ratnagiri turned violent
outcome: Project continued; protests persisted; Tabrez chowk became protest centre

name: Bhatta Parsaul farmers' land protest
city_or_district: Bhatta Parsaul, Greater Noida (Gautam Buddh Nagar)
trigger: Land acquisition for Yamuna Expressway at low compensation; farmers took transport officials hostage 2011-05-07, triggering police action
organisers: Local farmers (Manveer Tewatia); Rahul Gandhi/Congress and other parties joined
demands: Higher compensation; judicial inquiry into police action
state_response: Police operation 2011-05-07; DM and SSP injured; NHRC team visit; Rahul Gandhi detained 2011-05-11; Allahabad HC proceedings
outcome: Mayawati government revised land policy; incident fed into 2013 Land Acquisition Act debate

name: Baba Ramdev Ramlila Maidan fast and midnight police crackdown
trigger: Demand to bring back black money stashed abroad; breakdown of talks with ministers
organisers: Baba Ramdev / Bharat Swabhiman Trust
demands: Repatriation of black money; death penalty for corruption; withdrawal of Rs 1000/500 notes
state_response: Delhi Police midnight lathi charge and teargas 2011-06-04/05; Ramdev detained and flown to Haridwar; Supreme Court (Feb 2012) censured police and ordered compensation
outcome: Protest dispersed; Supreme Court held police action excessive

name: Maruti Suzuki Manesar workers' strikes 2011
trigger: Management refusal to recognise newly formed Maruti Suzuki Employees Union; dismissal of 11 workers 2011-06-06
organisers: Maruti Suzuki Employees Union (Sonu Gujjar); supported by AITUC, CITU, HMS
demands: Union recognition; reinstatement of dismissed/suspended workers; end to contract labour abuse
state_response: Haryana government mediation; police presence at plant; 'good conduct bond' dispute Aug-Sept; lockout and third strike Oct 2011
outcome: 13-day June strike ended 2011-06-17 without recognition; October occupation ended with settlement; Sonu Gujjar and 29 others resigned with severance
election_within_6_months: no (end date approximate - October settlement mid/late Oct 2011)

name: Anna Hazare Ramlila Maidan fast (India Against Corruption)
city_or_district: New Delhi (Ramlila Maidan); solidarity protests nationwide
trigger: Government's Lokpal Bill (Aug 2011) excluding PM and lower bureaucracy; Hazare's arrest on 2011-08-16 before fast
organisers: India Against Corruption (Anna Hazare, Arvind Kejriwal, Kiran Bedi, Prashant Bhushan)
demands: Jan Lokpal Bill covering PM, lower bureaucracy and Lokayuktas in states
crowd_press: tens of thousands in Delhi and other cities (press)
state_response: Hazare detained and sent to Tihar 2011-08-16, released; 15-day permission for Ramlila Maidan; Parliament 'sense of the House' resolution 2011-08-27
outcome: Fast ended 2011-08-28 after Parliament resolution; Lokpal Act eventually passed Dec 2013

name: Kudankulam anti-nuclear protests (PMANE) and Sept 2012 police firing
trigger: Hot run of Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant reactor; Fukushima fears; AERB clearance for fuel loading Aug 2012
organisers: People's Movement Against Nuclear Energy (S P Udayakumar)
demands: Closure/halt of Kudankulam plant
crowd_press: more than 8,000 (press)
state_response: Police lathi charge and teargas at Idinthakarai 2012-09-10; firing at Manapad; sedition and other cases against activists; TN government earlier (Sept 2011) asked Centre to halt work
outcome: Plant commissioned 2013; Supreme Court upheld project May 2013

name: Sakala Janula Samme (Telangana general strike)
city_or_district: Telangana districts (Hyderabad, Warangal, Karimnagar, Singareni belt)
trigger: Centre's inaction on Telangana after Srikrishna report; TJAC/KCR call for all-people's strike
organisers: Telangana Joint Action Committee, TRS, government employees' JAC, Singareni and RTC unions, teachers, lawyers
demands: Separate Telangana state
state_response: ESMA threats; talks with employee unions; coal output and public transport hit
outcome: Strike withdrawn after 42 days (2011-10-24) without statehood announcement

name: Mullaperiyar dam agitations (Kerala-Tamil Nadu)
trigger: Series of tremors in Idukki (Nov 2011) and reports of cracks in 116-year-old dam; Tamil Nadu refusal to lower water level
organisers: Kerala: Mullaperiyar Samara Samithi, UDF/LDF parties, Kerala MPs; Tamil Nadu: farmers' associations and parties
demands: Kerala: new dam and water level cut; Tamil Nadu: retain dam and raise level to 142 ft
state_response: Kerala police banned gatherings near dam; prohibitory orders at Kumily; hartals in Idukki; Kerala MPs protested in Parliament
outcome: Supreme Court empowered committee continued; SC in 2014 allowed TN to raise level
election_within_6_months: no (dates approximate - month-level; first/last of month used)

name: Nationwide general strike of central trade unions
trigger: Price rise, disinvestment, contractualisation, non-implementation of labour laws
organisers: 11 central trade unions incl. INTUC, BMS, AITUC, HMS, CITU, AIUTUC, TUCC, SEWA, AICCTU, UTUC, LPF plus ~5,000 unions
demands: Curb price rise; universal social security; minimum wage Rs 10,000; stop disinvestment; stop contractualisation; enforce labour laws
state_response: No special action reported; banks, ports, transport, mining hit
outcome: One-day strike; no policy change

name: Bharat bandh against petrol price hike
trigger: Petrol price hike of Rs 7.50 per litre on 2012-05-23
organisers: BJP-led NDA (L K Advani, Sharad Yadav) 'Bharat Bandh'; Left parties 'All India Protest Day'
demands: Rollback of petrol price hike
state_response: Arrests of protesters; stone pelting, arson and road blockades in Karnataka, Maharashtra, West Bengal
outcome: Partial rollback of about Rs 2 per litre on 2012-06-02

name: Maruti Suzuki Manesar plant violence and lockout
trigger: Dispute over suspension of a worker after altercation with supervisor on 2012-07-18; grievances over contract labour and wages
organisers: Maruti Suzuki Workers Union (Manesar)
demands: Reinstatement of suspended worker; end to contract labour discrimination
state_response: Lockout from 2012-07-21; 148 workers arrested; special security force; plant reopened 2012-08-21 with 300 workers; 546 permanent workers dismissed
outcome: 13 workers sentenced to life (2017), 117 acquitted

name: Assam (Bodoland Territorial Area Districts) Bodo-Muslim violence
trigger: Killing of four Bodo youths at Joypur, Kokrajhar on 2012-07-20 and retaliatory killings of Muslims 2012-07-21
organisers: Mobs; Bodo and Bengali-Muslim groups (not formally organised)
demands: Security; relief; (Bodo groups) eviction of 'illegal migrants'; (Muslim groups) protection and rehabilitation
state_response: Curfew; army deployment; ~400,000 displaced to relief camps; PM visit and relief package
outcome: Violence subsided by Sept 2012; long-term displacement; nationwide fallout (Azad Maidan, northeast exodus)

name: Azad Maidan protest and riot over Assam and Myanmar violence
trigger: Protest against violence on Muslims in Assam (BTAD) and Rohingya in Myanmar; circulated images on social media
organisers: Raza Academy, Sunni Jamiatul Ulema, Jamaat-e-Raza-e-Mustafa
demands: Action to protect Muslims in Assam and Myanmar
state_response: Police under Commissioner Arup Patnaik exercised restraint; later arrests; Amar Jawan memorial damaged; 45 policemen among 54 injured
outcome: Riot contained same day; Patnaik transferred; prosecutions followed

name: Exodus of northeastern migrants from Bengaluru and other cities
trigger: Rumours via SMS/MMS/social media of attacks on northeastern people after Assam violence, with a 'deadline' of Eid (2012-08-20)
organisers: None (rumour-driven panic)
demands: n/a (flight for safety)
crowd_press: more than 15,000 fled Bengaluru in two days (press); special trains to Guwahati
internet_shutdown: no (bulk SMS/MMS ban for 15 days from 2012-08-17)
state_response: Centre banned bulk SMS/MMS 15 days; Karnataka arrested rumour-mongers; special trains; CM and police appeals to stay
outcome: Exodus reversed by late August; return trains from Guwahati

name: Bharat bandh against FDI in retail and diesel price hike
trigger: Diesel price hike of Rs 5 per litre, cap of six subsidised LPG cylinders and decision to allow 51 per cent FDI in multi-brand retail (Sept 2012)
organisers: BJP-led NDA; Left parties; Samajwadi Party; TDP, BJD, JD(S), AIFB, RSP (Trinamool withdrew from UPA 2012-09-18)
demands: Rollback of diesel hike and LPG cap; withdrawal of FDI in retail
state_response: Opposition leaders including Mulayam Singh Yadav courted arrest; government notified FDI in retail the same day
outcome: No rollback; Assocham/CII estimated losses Rs 10,000-12,500 crore

name: Jan Satyagraha land-rights march (Ekta Parishad)
trigger: Non-implementation of 2007 land-reform commitments made after Janadesh 2007 march; landlessness among adivasis and dalits
organisers: Ekta Parishad (P V Rajagopal)
demands: National Land Reforms Act; homestead land rights; implementation of Forest Rights Act; land reform council
state_response: Rural Development Minister Jairam Ramesh negotiated en route
outcome: 10-point agreement signed at Agra 2012-10-11; march called off; draft National Land Reforms Policy 2013

name: Nirbhaya (Delhi gang-rape) protests
city_or_district: New Delhi (India Gate, Raisina Hill, Jantar Mantar); solidarity protests nationwide
trigger: Gang rape and fatal assault of a 23-year-old physiotherapy student on a bus on 2012-12-16
organisers: Largely spontaneous; students, women's groups, AAP, ABVP, SFI and others
demands: Death penalty/fast-track trial for rapists; police reform; safety for women; stronger rape law
crowd_press: thousands (press)
state_response: Teargas, water cannon and lathi charge at India Gate/Raisina Hill 2012-12-22/23; Section 144 and metro stations closed; Justice Verma Committee constituted 2012-12-23
outcome: Verma Committee report 2013-01-23; Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013; fast-track trial and convictions
election_within_6_months: no (Delhi assembly Dec 2013 is beyond 6 months; start date approximate - first major protests 2012-12-18 to 21)

name: Two-day nationwide general strike of central trade unions
trigger: Government inaction on price rise, disinvestment and violation of labour laws
organisers: 11 central trade unions (INTUC, BMS, AITUC, HMS, CITU, AIUTUC, TUCC, SEWA, AICCTU, UTUC, LPF)
demands: 10-point charter: price control, employment, enforce labour laws, universal social security, minimum wage Rs 10,000, stop disinvestment and contractualisation
state_response: Police action in Noida after factories and vehicles damaged; arrests
outcome: No policy change; violence in Noida Phase II

name: Tamil Nadu students' protests over Sri Lankan Tamils (UNHRC resolution)
city_or_district: Chennai (Loyola College and others), colleges statewide
trigger: Channel 4 footage of killing of Prabhakaran's son; US-sponsored UNHRC resolution on Sri Lanka; Loyola College students' hunger strike 2013-03-08 and their detention 2013-03-11
organisers: Students of ~40 arts and science colleges; Students Federation for Freedom of Tamil Eelam; later lawyers, IT workers, refugees
demands: India to vote for strong UNHRC resolution; referendum on Tamil Eelam; war-crimes probe; stop training Sri Lankan forces
crowd_organiser: ~1 million at pre-vote protest (Tamil advocacy claim)
state_response: Police detained Loyola strikers; colleges closed; TN assembly resolution 2013-03-22 demanding referendum; DMK quit UPA 2013-03-19
outcome: India voted for UNHRC resolution 2013-03-21; protests tapered by early April

name: Niyamgiri anti-Vedanta bauxite mining movement (Supreme Court and gram sabha phase)
trigger: Supreme Court judgment (April 2013) referring Vedanta/OMC bauxite mining to gram sabhas; Dongria Kondh religious and livelihood claims
organisers: Niyamgiri Suraksha Samiti; Dongria Kondh villagers; supported by Survival International, Amnesty
demands: No mining on Niyamgiri; recognition of Niyam Raja worship rights
state_response: Supreme Court ordered gram sabha consultations; Odisha government held 12 gram sabhas July-Aug 2013 under judicial observation
outcome: All 12 gram sabhas rejected mining; MoEF denied clearance Jan 2014; movement began 2003-04 but earlier phase not sourced here
election_within_6_months: no (start date is first of month - SC judgment April 2013, day not in sources)

name: Delhi protests over rape of five-year-old (Gandhi Nagar)
city_or_district: New Delhi (Police HQ ITO, AIIMS, Home Minister's and Sonia Gandhi's residences)
trigger: Rape and torture of a five-year-old girl in Gandhi Nagar discovered 2013-04-15; allegations police offered bribe to family; ACP slapped a protesting schoolgirl
organisers: AAP, SFI, ABVP, students and citizens
demands: Resignation of Police Commissioner Neeraj Kumar; police accountability; justice for victim
crowd_press: over 300 at Police HQ on 2013-04-20 (press)
state_response: Police barricades and pushing back of protesters; ACP suspended for slapping protester; accused arrested in Bihar
outcome: Commissioner did not resign; two accused convicted 2014
election_within_6_months: no (Delhi assembly Dec 2013 is beyond 6 months; end date approximate)

name: Samaikyandhra agitation against Telangana bifurcation
trigger: CWC/UPA decision of 2013-07-30 to create Telangana state
organisers: APNGO (Ashok Babu), Samaikyandhra JAC, Seemandhra MPs/MLAs, YSRCP, Lagadapati Rajagopal
demands: Keep Andhra Pradesh united; alternatively protect Hyderabad status and water/power shares
state_response: Spontaneous bandh 2013-07-31; indefinite employee and power-sector strike Aug-Oct 2013; Centre pressed on with bill (introduced Feb 2014)
outcome: AP Reorganisation Act passed Feb 2014; Telangana formed 2014-06-02 (agitation continued to Feb 2014; end date truncated to catalogue period)
election_within_6_months: yes (Lok Sabha and AP assembly Apr-May 2014)

name: Gorkhaland indefinite bandh 2013
trigger: Centre's approval of Telangana state (2013-07-30/31) seen as precedent for Gorkhaland; Bimal Gurung quit as GTA chief executive
organisers: Gorkha Janmukti Morcha (Bimal Gurung)
demands: Separate state of Gorkhaland; tripartite talks
state_response: West Bengal government refused talks on statehood; detentions of GJM supporters; Calcutta HC declared bandh illegal; staggered closures ~44 days
outcome: Bandh suspended Sept 2013 pending talks; no statehood

name: Kishtwar communal clashes and Jammu protests
city_or_district: Kishtwar, Jammu, Udhampur, Kathua, Samba, Bhaderwah
trigger: Altercation between a biker and Eid prayer procession in Kishtwar 2013-08-09 escalating into Hindu-Muslim clashes
organisers: Mobs in Kishtwar; BJP, VHP and Jammu groups for bandh
demands: Action against rioters; resignation of MoS Home Sajjad Kichloo; judicial probe
state_response: Curfew in Kishtwar and seven of ten Jammu districts; army deployed; MoS Home Sajjad Kichloo resigned 2013-08-12; judicial probe ordered
outcome: Curfew lifted gradually; judicial commission report later tabled

name: Muzaffarnagar riots and aftermath (mahapanchayats, relief-camp protests)
trigger: Killing of three youths at Kawal village 2013-08-27 after alleged harassment incident; Jat mahapanchayat at Nangla Mandaur 2013-09-07 and attacks on returning participants
organisers: Bharatiya Kisan Union and khap panchayats (mahapanchayat); BJP leaders (Sangeet Som, Suresh Rana, Sanjeev Balyan) named in FIRs; Muslim groups
demands: Mahapanchayat: 'Beti Bahu Bachao', action against accused; displaced Muslims: security, compensation, rehabilitation
crowd_press: over 100,000 at 2013-09-07 mahapanchayat (press/Wikipedia-derived)
state_response: Curfew; army deployed 2013-09-08; ~50,955 displaced in state-run relief camps; SIT; Sahai judicial commission; NSA on BJP MLAs
outcome: Riots ended Sept 2013; relief camp deaths and displacement continued into winter; political polarisation before 2014 polls

name: Protests against Supreme Court Section 377 verdict
city_or_district: New Delhi (Jantar Mantar), Mumbai, Bengaluru, Pune, Kolkata
trigger: Supreme Court judgment in Suresh Kumar Koushal v Naz Foundation (2013-12-11) recriminalising consensual same-sex relations
organisers: LGBT groups and allies (Naz Foundation, Voices Against 377, Humsafar Trust, Queer collectives)
demands: Review/overturning of verdict; repeal of Section 377
crowd_press: hundreds at Jantar Mantar (press)
state_response: No police action reported; government filed review petition Dec 2013
outcome: Review dismissed Jan 2014; curative petition; Section 377 read down in Navtej Johar 2018

name: FTII students' strike against chairman Gajendra Chauhan
city_or_district: Film and Television Institute of India, Pune; Jantar Mantar
trigger: Appointment of actor and BJP member Gajendra Chauhan as FTII chairman (June 2015), seen as politically motivated and lacking credentials
organisers: FTII Students' Association; alumni and film personalities
demands: Removal of Chauhan and other society nominees; autonomy of institute
violence: none (students detained during midnight police action on campus Aug 2015)
state_response: I&B Ministry held talks; police detained students in Aug 2015; Chauhan kept in post
outcome: 139-day strike called off 28 Oct 2015; students vowed to continue seeking removal; Chauhan's tenure ended Mar 2017 and Anupam Kher appointed

name: Ex-servicemen's One Rank One Pension agitation
trigger: Delay in implementing One Rank One Pension promised in 2014; veterans began relay hunger strike 15 June 2015
organisers: United Front of Ex-Servicemen / Indian Ex-Servicemen Movement (Maj Gen Satbir Singh)
demands: Implement OROP as per Koshyari committee definition; annual equalisation
violence: none (police manhandled protesters during eviction attempt Aug 2015)
state_response: Govt announced OROP scheme on 5 Sep 2015 after 84 days (with 5-yearly equalisation); veterans called it 'one rank five pensions'
outcome: Partial win; protest continued at Jantar Mantar in reduced form until eviction Oct 2017

name: Patidar (Patel) reservation agitation
trigger: Patidar community demand for OBC status; Hardik Patel's brief arrest after 25 Aug 2015 GMDC rally triggered statewide violence
organisers: Patidar Anamat Andolan Samiti (PAAS), Hardik Patel; Sardar Patel Group
demands: OBC status/reservation for Patidars in jobs and education
crowd_press: c. 400,000 at GMDC ground on 25 Aug 2015 (estimate cited via Wikipedia)
state_response: Curfew in several cities, Army called in; police firing (e.g. Gadh village near Palanpur); 203 police injured
outcome: Agitation subsided; Gujarat announced EBC 10% quota 2016 (struck down); Hardik Patel sedition case; 14 deaths acknowledged
sources: start date approximated to first of month (rallies began July 2015) | https://www.thequint.com/elections/gujarat-election/hardik-patel-patidar-andolan-movement-protests-bjp-families-of-14-who-died-killed-police-firing-2015-2017-2022 | https://www.deccanherald.com/india/father-offered-crores-stop-hardik-2051067 | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patidar_reservation_agitation

name: Manipur ILP / three bills protests (Churachandpur)
trigger: Manipur assembly passed three bills on 31 Aug 2015 (Protection of Manipur People Bill; MLR&LR 7th Amendment; Shops and Establishments 2nd Amendment) after Imphal valley ILP agitation; hill tribes saw bills as threat to land rights
organisers: Joint Committee on Inner Line Permit System (valley); Joint Action Committee Against Anti-Tribal Bills (Churachandpur hills)
demands: Valley: ILP-type regulation of outsiders; Hills: withdrawal of the three bills, later 'separate administration'
deaths: 9 (eight young men and an 11-year-old boy, Churachandpur)
state_response: Curfew in Churachandpur; four tribal MLAs resigned; President withheld assent to Protection of Manipur People Bill (2016)
outcome: Bodies of the nine kept unburied for 632 days until MoU with BJP government and burial in May 2017

name: Central trade unions' nationwide general strike (Bharat Bandh) 2015
city_or_district: Kolkata; Kerala; Bengaluru; Delhi; industrial belts
trigger: Proposed labour-law amendments and land acquisition ordinance; talks with government failed
organisers: 10 central trade unions (INTUC, AITUC, HMS, CITU, AIUTUC, TUCC, SEWA, AICCTU, LPF, UTUC); BMS opted out after 26-27 Aug talks
demands: 12-point charter: withdraw labour-law amendments and land ordinance; stop privatisation/FDI in railways, insurance, defence; minimum wage; universal PDS
state_response: Two rounds of government talks on 12-point charter failed; BMS withdrew after partial assurances; normal life hit in West Bengal, Tripura, Kerala, Karnataka
outcome: Banking and transport worst hit; no concessions; template for later annual strikes

name: Pembilai Orumai women tea workers' strike (Munnar)
trigger: Kanan Devan Hills Plantations cut annual bonus from 20% to 10%; women pluckers struck on 6 Sep 2015 excluding male union leaders
organisers: Pembilai Orumai (women's unity collective, later a union)
demands: 20% bonus; daily wage hike from Rs 232 to Rs 500
crowd_press: about 5,000 workers, mostly women (Business Standard/PTI)
state_response: CM Oommen Chandy chaired marathon talks; management conceded 20% bonus (11.67% ex gratia + 8.33% statutory)
outcome: Nine-day strike ended 13 Sep 2015 with bonus win; wage talks continued; Pembilai Orumai contested local polls

name: Dadri lynching aftermath protests
city_or_district: Bisara village, Dadri (Gautam Buddh Nagar); Delhi
trigger: Mohammad Akhlaq (52) lynched by a mob at Bisara, Dadri on 28 Sep 2015 over rumours of cow slaughter announced from a temple loudspeaker; son Danish critically injured
organisers: Civil society; writers' 'award wapsi' (Nayantara Sahgal, Ashok Vajpeyi and others returned Sahitya Akademi awards); opposition leaders (Kejriwal, Rahul Gandhi) visited; counter-protests by villagers against arrests
demands: Justice for Akhlaq; action against communal politics; (counter) release of accused
violence: clashes (villagers protesting arrests burnt vehicles and vandalised shops; police fired in air; one injured)
state_response: Arrests of accused; heavy police deployment at Bisara; UP government compensation; IAF relocated family
outcome: Trial pending for years; triggered nationwide 'award wapsi' movement and debate ahead of Bihar polls
election_within_6_months: yes: Bihar assembly Oct-Nov 2015 (BJP called outrage propaganda ahead of Bihar polls)
sources: end date approximated (award wapsi through Oct 2015) | https://www.aljazeera.com/indepth/features/2017/09/lynching-changed-india-170927084018325.html | https://www.epw.in/journal/commentary/vigilantism-trumps-justice.html | https://www.thequint.com/news/india/dadri-lynching-five-years-mohammad-akhlaq | https://www.oneindia.com/feature/flashback-2015-from-award-wapsi-orop-protest-modi-govt-bjp-1964423.html | https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/nation/iaf-steps-in-wants-to-shift-its-man-s-family-141312

name: Bargari sacrilege protests and Behbal Kalan/Kotkapura police firing
city_or_district: Bargari, Behbal Kalan and Kotkapura (Faridkot); statewide
trigger: Torn pages of a Guru Granth Sahib 'bir' (stolen June 2015) found at Bargari on 12 Oct 2015; Sikh protesters blocked roads; police fired at Kotkapura and Behbal Kalan on 14 Oct
organisers: Sikh sangat and organisations; later Bargari Insaaf Morcha
demands: Arrest of sacrilege culprits; action against police officers; justice for the two killed
deaths: 2 (Gurjeet Singh and Krishan Bhagwan Singh, Behbal Kalan, 14 Oct 2015)
state_response: Statewide protests; Zora Singh and Ranjit Singh commissions; SITs chargesheeted police incl. then DGP Sumedh Saini; IG arrested 2019
outcome: Cases pending for years; issue central to 2017 and 2022 Punjab elections

name: Occupy UGC protest against scrapping of non-NET fellowship
trigger: UGC decision (Oct 2015) to discontinue non-NET fellowships (Rs 5,000 MPhil / Rs 8,000 PhD per month) for research scholars
organisers: Students of JNU, DU, Jamia, Ambedkar University, IP University; AISA, SFI and other student groups
demands: Restore and expand non-NET fellowship; oppose WTO/GATS commitments in higher education
crowd_press: hundreds of students occupied UGC office on 21 Oct 2015 (The Wire)
violence: clashes (Delhi Police lathicharged protesters 23 and 27 Oct; at least two hospitalised)
state_response: HRD ministry set up review committee; police lathicharge and detentions; sit-in outside UGC continued for weeks
outcome: Fellowship continued for existing scholars with review; protest dwindled by Dec 2015; fed into later campus mobilisations

name: Rohith Vemula protests (Hyderabad Central University)
city_or_district: University of Hyderabad, Gachibowli; nationwide campuses
trigger: Suicide of Dalit PhD scholar Rohith Vemula on 17 Jan 2016 after suspension of five ASA students from hostel; alleged ministerial pressure
organisers: Ambedkar Students' Association; Joint Action Committee for Social Justice; student groups nationwide
demands: Rohith Act against caste discrimination; removal/arrest of VC Appa Rao Podile and minister Bandaru Dattatreya
violence: clashes (police action on campus when VC returned 22 Mar 2016; students arrested)
state_response: SC/ST (PoA) case registered against Dattatreya and VC; HRD ministry inquiry (Roopanwal commission); police action on campus March 2016
outcome: VC remained in post; Roopanwal report (2017) disputed; nationwide campus mobilisation and 'Rohith Act' demand unmet
