name: Kapu agitation (Tuni)
trigger: Kapu Garjana rally demanding TDP honour 2014 promise of BC status for Kapus; turned violent
organisers: Mudragada Padmanabham; Kapu community organisations
demands: Inclusion of Kapus in Backward Classes list
state_response: Police reinforcements; 63 cases against Mudragada; later house arrests during his hunger strikes
outcome: Ratnachal Express coaches and two police stations burnt; NH-16 blocked; demand unresolved, Mudragada continued fasts 2016-18

name: Jat reservation agitation
trigger: Demand for OBC quota for Jats after Supreme Court struck down central Jat OBC inclusion (2015); agitation turned violent 18 Feb 2016
organisers: All India Jat Arakshan Sangharsh Samiti (AIJASS)
demands: OBC reservation for Jats in government jobs and higher education
internet_shutdown: yes: Rohtak (mobile internet/SMS suspended 18 Feb-1 Mar 2016); Kaithal (until 17 Mar 2016)
state_response: Curfew, Army deployed; Prakash Singh Committee appointed 25 Feb 2016, report (13 May 2016) indicted 80 officials
outcome: Haryana enacted Backward Classes Act 2016 giving Jats quota (later stayed by High Court); SIT registered 986+ cases; damage estimated in thousands of crores

name: JNU sedition row protests
city_or_district: Jawaharlal Nehru University; Patiala House court
trigger: Campus event on Afzal Guru hanging (9 Feb); arrest of JNUSU president Kanhaiya Kumar for sedition (12 Feb)
organisers: JNU Students' Union; JNU Teachers' Association; DSU; solidarity from universities nationwide
demands: Release of arrested students; drop sedition charges; defend academic freedom
crowd_press: thousands marched in Delhi 18 Feb 2016 (Al Jazeera)
violence: clashes (lawyers assaulted journalists and Kumar at Patiala House court 15 and 17 Feb)
state_response: Sedition arrests of Kanhaiya Kumar, Umar Khalid, Anirban Bhattacharya; university inquiry
outcome: Kanhaiya Kumar granted interim bail 2 Mar 2016; Delhi Police chargesheet filed only in Jan 2019

name: Hyderabad Central University protests on VC Appa Rao's return
trigger: Return of VC Appa Rao Podile from leave on 22 Mar 2016 two months after Rohith Vemula's death
organisers: Joint Action Committee for Social Justice; Ambedkar Students' Association; faculty supporters
demands: Removal and arrest of VC; Rohith Act
violence: clashes (CRPF/RAF lathicharge; VC's lodge ransacked; c. 36 students and 3 faculty detained overnight; 25 students and 2 faculty jailed)
state_response: Police action on campus; arrests; university shut mess, drinking water, power and internet on 23 Mar; campus lockdown
outcome: Students and faculty granted bail (28 Mar); VC remained in post; international academic statements of support

name: Bengaluru garment workers' PF protest
trigger: Central notification (10 Feb 2016) restricting withdrawal of employer's PF contribution until age 58; spread via Kannada daily report 16 Apr
organisers: Largely spontaneous, mostly women garment workers; GATWU and unions joined later
demands: Withdraw PF withdrawal restrictions
crowd_press: at least 50,000 workers, some estimates 1 lakh (fact-finding report/press)
violence: clashes (stone-throwing, lathicharge; at least 15 buses torched and a police station attacked on 19 Apr)
state_response: Police lathicharge and tear gas; Mysuru highway blocked 10 hours; Labour Minister Dattatreya cancelled the notification on 19 Apr 2016
outcome: Full rollback of PF notification within two days
election_within_6_months: yes: Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Assam assembly Apr-May 2016 (not Karnataka)

name: Protests over Jisha's rape-murder (Perumbavoor)
city_or_district: Perumbavoor (Ernakulam); Government Law College Ernakulam; statewide
trigger: Rape and murder of 30-year-old Dalit law student Jisha at her home in Perumbavoor on 28 Apr 2016, 18 days before assembly polls; slow police response
organisers: Law students of Government Law College Ernakulam; women's and Dalit groups; opposition LDF and BJP
demands: Swift arrest; justice; accountability of UDF government and police
state_response: UDF government formed special team; new LDF government arrested migrant worker Ameerul Islam in June 2016
outcome: Case became election issue; accused convicted Dec 2017 (life, enhanced to death by HC 2024)

name: Kashmir unrest after Burhan Wani killing
city_or_district: Kashmir Valley (Srinagar, Anantnag, Kulgam, Pulwama, Shopian)
trigger: Killing of Hizbul Mujahideen commander Burhan Wani by security forces on 8 Jul 2016
organisers: Separatist leadership (Hurriyat/JRL protest calendars); largely spontaneous street protests
demands: Azadi/self-determination; end to killings; withdrawal of forces
deaths: 86+ (HT toll by Sep 2016); >90 by end of unrest (Wikipedia: >96)
internet_shutdown: yes: Kashmir Valley (mobile internet and communication blackouts over the unrest period)
state_response: 53 consecutive days of curfew (lifted 31 Aug 2016); pellet guns, tear gas; mass detentions under PSA; schools shut
outcome: Unrest tapered by Feb 2017; >15,000 civilians and >4,000 security personnel injured; no political settlement

name: Una Dalit flogging protests and Dalit Asmita Yatra
trigger: Cow-vigilantes beat four Dalit youths with sticks and iron rods at Mota Samadhiyala, Una (11 Jul 2016), tied them to a vehicle and paraded them; video went viral
organisers: Una Dalit Atyachar Ladat Samiti (Jignesh Mevani); Rashtriya Dalit Adhikar Manch; Dalit organisations across Gujarat
demands: Arrest and conviction of attackers; land for Dalit families; end to cow-vigilante violence; freedom from caste-based occupations
crowd_press: thousands joined the 10-day Dalit Asmita Yatra (Ahmedabad to Una) culminating 15 Aug 2016 (Al Jazeera)
violence: clashes (statewide protests and bus arson in July 2016; several Dalit youths attempted suicide in protest)
deaths: n/a (one police constable's death during July protests reported elsewhere; not confirmed in cited sources)
state_response: Accused arrested; CM Anandiben Patel resigned in Aug 2016 amid Patidar and Dalit unrest
outcome: Dalits at Una pledged to abandon carcass disposal; Mevani elected MLA Dec 2017; trial court convicted 5 and acquitted 38 in 2025

name: Maratha Kranti Morcha (silent marches and 2018 quota stir)
trigger: Rape-murder of a Maratha minor at Kopardi, Ahmednagar (13 Jul 2016); broader demand for Maratha reservation
organisers: Maratha Kranti Morcha (leaderless coordination committees)
demands: Justice in Kopardi case; Maratha reservation in jobs/education; amendments to SC/ST Atrocities Act; farm relief
crowd_organiser: over 5 lakh expected for Mumbai march 9 Aug 2017 (organiser expectation reported by Free Press Journal)
crowd_press: around half a million in Mumbai 9 Aug 2017 (press); tens of thousands at Aurangabad 9 Aug 2016
violence: clashes (2016-17 marches silent and peaceful; July-Aug 2018 phase saw violence and bandh)
state_response: State committee on reservation; State Backward Class Commission report Nov 2018
outcome: Maharashtra passed SEBC reservation Act (Nov 2018); struck down by Supreme Court May 2021

name: Central trade unions' nationwide general strike 2016
city_or_district: Kerala; West Bengal; Karnataka; Tripura; Haryana
trigger: Labour-law reform agenda, privatisation and FDI; government's minimum-wage offer (Rs 350/day) rejected
organisers: Joint platform of 10 central trade unions (INTUC, AITUC, HMS, CITU, AIUTUC, TUCC, SEWA, AICCTU, LPF, UTUC); BMS stayed away
demands: Minimum wage Rs 18,000/month; no labour-law dilution; stop privatisation and FDI; social security; 12-point charter: statutory minimum wage, no labour-law dilution, halt privatisation/FDI in PSUs, universal social security, end contractualisation, price control
state_response: Government announced minimum-wage hike and bonus arrears before strike; BMS withdrew after agreement
outcome: No further concessions; banking, transport affected in Left states
election_within_6_months: yes: UP, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Goa, Manipur assembly Feb-Mar 2017

name: Cauvery water protests and Bengaluru violence
trigger: Supreme Court orders (5 and 12 Sep 2016) directing Karnataka to release Cauvery water (12,000 cusecs/day) to Tamil Nadu amid deficit monsoon
organisers: Pro-Kannada organisations (Karnataka Rakshana Vedike and others); farmers' groups in Mandya; Karnataka bandh 9 Sep
demands: Refuse/limit water release; protect Karnataka farmers
deaths: 2 (one shot by police at Hegganahalli; one died of injuries fleeing police)
state_response: Curfew in parts of Bengaluru; Section 144; thousands of police deployed; hundreds detained; police later alleged extortion rackets behind arson
outcome: More than 100 vehicles burnt incl. c. 30 TN-registered buses at a depot; Metro suspended; violence subsided in two days; Cauvery Management Authority formed 2018

name: Protests against CNT/SPT Act amendments
trigger: Raghubar Das government's ordinance/bills (2016) amending Chota Nagpur Tenancy and Santhal Pargana Tenancy Acts to allow non-agricultural use/acquisition of tribal land; police fired on protest 22-23 Oct 2016
organisers: Adivasi organisations; opposition JMM, JVM, Congress; church bodies; Adivasi Adhikar Manch
demands: Withdraw CNT/SPT amendments; protect tribal land rights; justice for Khunti firing
deaths: 1 (Abhram Mundu, Khunti, Oct 2016; some reports cite more deaths across protests)
state_response: Police firing in Khunti; arrests of protesters; Governor returned the bills (June 2017)
outcome: Government withdrew the amendment bills in Aug 2017 after Governor's return; fed into Pathalgadi movement

name: Jan Aakrosh Diwas protests against demonetisation
trigger: Demonetisation of Rs 500/1000 notes (8 Nov 2016) and cash shortage hardships
organisers: Left Front (Bharat Bandh in Kerala, Tripura, West Bengal); Congress, TMC, AAP, SP, BSP (Aakrosh Diwas protests without bandh)
demands: Reversal/relief measures for demonetisation; relief for farmers and small traders
violence: none (Left activists partly halted rail and road traffic in Bihar)
state_response: Government defended policy; 12-hour shutdown observed in Kerala and Tripura; little impact in West Bengal and Karnataka
outcome: Lukewarm response outside Left-ruled states; no policy change; opposition divided over bandh call
election_within_6_months: yes: UP, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Goa, Manipur assembly Feb-Mar 2017

name: Pro-jallikattu protests (Marina Beach)
trigger: Supreme Court ban on jallikattu; PETA litigation; refusal to permit Pongal 2017 events
organisers: Leaderless youth mobilisation via social media; student groups
demands: Permanent legal protection for jallikattu; ban on PETA
crowd_press: 15,000 along 6 km of Marina on 20 Jan 2017 (Citizen Matters)
violence: clashes (police eviction on 23 Jan, stone-pelting, vehicles burnt)
state_response: Police watched for a week then evicted Marina crowd on 23 Jan with lathicharge and tear gas; cases later withdrawn against 26,460 persons
outcome: Ordinance 21 Jan 2017; Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Tamil Nadu Amendment) Act passed 23 Jan 2017; jallikattu resumed

name: Ramjas College clashes (Delhi University)
city_or_district: Ramjas College, North Campus, Delhi University
trigger: ABVP disrupted a Ramjas seminar 'Cultures of Protest' (21 Feb 2017) over invitation to JNU's Umar Khalid; AISA-SFI march to police station attacked 22 Feb
organisers: ABVP (disruption); AISA, SFI and DU teachers (protest march); Gurmehar Kaur's social-media campaign; 'Save DU' march 28 Feb
demands: (Left) action against ABVP violence, free speech on campus; (ABVP) ban 'anti-national' speakers
violence: clashes (students, teachers and police injured in stone-pelting and assaults 22 Feb)
state_response: Police deployment; FIRs; counter 'Tiranga march' by ABVP
outcome: Khalid's talk cancelled; nationwide debate on campus free speech; no major disciplinary outcome

name: Tamil Nadu farmers' protest at Jantar Mantar
trigger: 2016-17 drought in Tamil Nadu (worst rainfall in 140 years), farmer suicides and crop loan distress
organisers: National South Indian River Interlinking Agriculturalists Association (P. Ayyakannu)
demands: Farm loan waiver; drought relief package; river interlinking; Cauvery Management Board; remunerative prices
state_response: No meeting granted by PM; Madras High Court ordered cooperative loan waiver (on 22nd day of protest); TN CM assurance 23 Apr
outcome: First phase suspended after 41 days; protest resumed in phases (141 days in total); partial state loan waiver

name: Saharanpur (Shabbirpur) caste violence and Bhim Army protests
city_or_district: Shabbirpur, Saharanpur; Jantar Mantar, New Delhi
trigger: Rajput procession for Maharana Pratap Jayanti entered Dalit colony of Shabbirpur on 5 May 2017; one Rajput died, 25 Dalit houses burnt; later attacks on Dalits after Mayawati's 23 May visit
organisers: Bhim Army (Chandrashekhar Azad 'Ravan'); BSP (Mayawati rally 23 May)
demands: Justice and compensation for Shabbirpur Dalits; arrest of attackers; end to caste atrocities
crowd_press: thousands at Bhim Army rally in Delhi 21 May; c. 5,000 at Jantar Mantar 22 May (Caravan)
deaths: 2 (one Rajput on 5 May; one Dalit killed after 23 May rally)
state_response: RAF deployed; Chandrashekhar arrested 8 Jun 2017 from Dalhousie; detained under NSA Nov 2017 after HC bail
outcome: Bhim Army emerged as national Dalit organisation; Chandrashekhar released Sept 2018

name: Pathalgadi movement (Khunti)
trigger: Munda Adivasi villages erected stone plaques citing Fifth Schedule/PESA to assert gram sabha autonomy against land acquisition and CNT Act amendments; police entry into Ghaghra on 26 Jun 2018
organisers: Village gram sabhas; Adivasi Mahasabha; activists invoking PESA
demands: Gram sabha autonomy; no outsider entry/land acquisition without consent; release of detained villagers
crowd_press: c. 2,000 villagers opposed c. 500 police at Ghaghra 26 Jun 2018 (Participedia/Pulitzer)
state_response: Sedition cases against more than 10,000 people in Khunti (June 2017-July 2018); police raids; Fr Stan Swamy among those named
outcome: Movement suppressed; Hemant Soren govt announced withdrawal of Pathalgadi sedition cases (Dec 2019)
sources: start/end dates approximated to month | https://participedia.net/case/12525 | https://www.epw.in/engage/article/pathalgadi-movement-nation-autonomy-rights-adivasi-jharkhand | https://pulitzercenter.org/stories/pathalgadi-assertion-adivasi-rights-over-land | https://www.newsclick.in/jharkhand-every-10-adivasi-khunti-dist-charged-sedition-resorting-pathalgarhi

name: Maharashtra farmers' strike (Puntamba)
trigger: Price crash and debt; farmers of Puntamba called statewide strike from 1 June 2017 halting milk and vegetable supplies
organisers: Kisan Kranti Jan Andolan / Sukanu Samiti; farmer groups; Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana
demands: Complete loan waiver; MSP at Swaminathan formula; milk price; pensions
crowd_organiser: 1.5 crore farmers claimed (press reporting strike call)
violence: clashes (road blockades, milk tankers emptied, some vandalism)
state_response: CM Fadnavis announced waiver for small/marginal farmers (3 June) then Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Krishi Samman Yojana (24 June) waiving loans up to Rs 1.5 lakh
outcome: Rs 34,000 crore waiver for 89 lakh farmers announced 24 June 2017; strike wound down mid-June
sources: end date approximated (strike wound down around 11 June) | https://www.deccanherald.com/india/maharashtra-agrees-to-waive-farmers-loans-593795.html | https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/nation/maharashtra-cm-announces-rs-34-000-crore-debt-relief-to-farmers-427016 | https://www.pressreader.com/india/the-free-press-journal/20170601/281479276374644 | https://www.pressreader.com/india/business-standard/20170613/281728384499659

name: Mandsaur farmers' agitation and police firing
trigger: Crash in onion/pulse prices; 10-day farmers' strike from 1 June; police fired on protesters 6 June killing farmers
organisers: Rashtriya Kisan Mazdoor Sangh; Bharatiya Kisan Sangh; local farmer groups
demands: Loan waiver; Swaminathan-formula MSP; remunerative prices
deaths: 6 (5 in police firing, 1 allegedly beaten by police)
state_response: Curfew; judicial inquiry (Jain Commission gave police clean chit June 2018); Rs 1 crore compensation per family, govt jobs; CM fast
outcome: Compensation paid; nationwide farmer mobilisation; issue cited in BJP's Dec 2018 MP defeat

name: Gorkhaland agitation 2017 (Darjeeling)
trigger: West Bengal order making Bengali compulsory in schools (May 2017); GJM revived statehood demand; indefinite bandh from 15 June 2017
organisers: Gorkha Janmukti Morcha (Bimal Gurung); Gorkhaland Movement Coordination Committee
demands: Separate state of Gorkhaland
internet_shutdown: yes: Darjeeling hills (state cut internet services and blocked local TV channels for the duration of the unrest)
state_response: Army and paramilitary deployed; internet shutdown; cases against Bimal Gurung; talks with breakaway Binay Tamang faction
outcome: 104-day strike called off 26 Sep 2017 after Home Minister Rajnath Singh's appeal; GJM split; no statehood; tourism and tea badly hit

name: Surat textile traders' GST strike
trigger: 5% GST on textiles/job-work from 1 July 2017 on previously untaxed trade
organisers: GST Sangharsh Samiti; Federation of Surat Textile Traders Association (c. 75,000 traders)
demands: Exempt textiles from GST or roll back 5% rate; simplify compliance
crowd_organiser: 75,000 traders on strike; c. 15 lakh workers idled (traders' claim)
violence: clashes (stone-pelting and lathicharge at Surat market on 8 Jul)
state_response: FM Arun Jaitley met traders 17 Jul and promised to place issue before GST Council (5 Aug)
outcome: Strike called off 18 Jul after 15-22 days (press counts vary); losses c. Rs 5,000 crore claimed; GST rate unchanged

name: Panchkula violence after Dera Sacha Sauda chief's conviction
trigger: CBI court conviction of Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh for rape (25 Aug 2017); tens of thousands of followers had gathered in Panchkula
organisers: Dera Sacha Sauda followers (tens of thousands had gathered in Panchkula ahead of the verdict)
demands: Release of Dera chief
deaths: 36-38 (HT: 36 dead, 423 injured; Tribune: 37 killed in Panchkula; DH early count 28)
internet_shutdown: yes: Haryana and Punjab (mobile internet suspended around the verdict; see Wikipedia summary) - not detailed in cited news snippets
state_response: Curfew in Panchkula and Sirsa; Army deployed; Punjab and Haryana HC criticised state for allowing gathering; Dera assets attached for damages; Honeypreet and 39 others charged
outcome: Ram Rahim jailed; 74 vehicles burnt; acquittals in several riot cases by 2020-2025 for want of evidence

name: Sikar farmers' agitation (Rajasthan)
city_or_district: Sikar; Jhunjhunu; Bikaner; Nagaur; Churu; Hanumangarh; Sri Ganganagar
trigger: Low prices, debt, cattle-trade restrictions; AIKS called indefinite mahapadav at Sikar Krishi Mandi from 1 Sep 2017
organisers: All India Kisan Sabha (Amra Ram, Pema Ram)
demands: Loan waiver; MSP at Swaminathan formula; pension; lifting of cattle-trade restrictions; electricity tariff rollback
crowd_organiser: thousands at Sikar mandi; rasta roko across c. 20 districts (AIKS)
state_response: Vasundhara Raje government held four rounds of talks 12-14 Sep; accepted loan waiver up to Rs 50,000 and other demands
outcome: Agitation called off after 13 days with written agreement

name: Anti-NEET protests after Anitha's suicide
trigger: Suicide (1 Sep 2017) of 17-year-old Dalit student S. Anitha, a petitioner against NEET, who scored 1176/1200 in state board but failed NEET cut-off
organisers: Student groups; Tamil nationalist and political parties (DMK, Left, VCK); spontaneous youth protests
demands: Exempt Tamil Nadu from NEET; justice for Anitha; state-board-based medical admission
crowd_press: hundreds of protesters staged rallies and road blockades across TN on 2 Sep (press)
violence: clashes (road blockades; SC directed TN to book protesters disrupting normal life)
state_response: Rs 7 lakh ex-gratia and govt job to family; SC ordered arrests of disruptive protesters (8 Sep); Centre refused NEET exemption ordinance
outcome: NEET remained; TN passed NEET-exemption bill 2021 (returned by Governor)

name: Bhima Koregaon violence and Maharashtra bandh
trigger: Attack on Dalits gathered for bicentenary of Battle of Koregaon (1 Jan 2018); one man killed; Dalit groups called statewide bandh 3 Jan
organisers: Bharipa Bahujan Mahasangh (Prakash Ambedkar) backed by c. 250 groups
demands: Arrest of Milind Ekbote and Sambhaji Bhide; justice for victims
state_response: Judicial inquiry commission; Ekbote arrested Mar 2018; from June 2018 'Elgar Parishad' UAPA arrests of activists
outcome: Bandh called off 3 Jan evening; Mumbai transport paralysed; long-running Elgar Parishad case

name: Karni Sena protests against film Padmaavat
state: Rajasthan; Gujarat; Haryana; Madhya Pradesh; Uttar Pradesh; Maharashtra; Bihar
trigger: Release of Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Padmaavat (25 Jan 2018) alleged to insult Rajput queen Padmini; SC struck down state bans on 18 Jan
organisers: Shri Rajput Karni Sena (Lokendra Singh Kalvi) and allied Rajput groups
demands: Ban on film; cuts/renaming
violence: clashes (school bus attacked and vehicles torched in Gurugram 24 Jan; stone-pelting and road blockades in Surat and elsewhere; 35 cases across seven states)
state_response: About 150 agitators arrested in 4 days before release; SC refused to allow state bans (Rajasthan, MP, Haryana, Gujarat); police investigation of bus attack
outcome: Film released 25 Jan 2018 under security; Karni Sena later withdrew opposition

name: Anti-Sterlite protest and Thoothukudi police firing
trigger: Pollution from Vedanta's Sterlite copper smelter and proposed expansion; 100th-day march to Collectorate on 22 May 2018
organisers: Anti-Sterlite People's Movement; village committees; traders' associations
demands: Permanent closure of Sterlite copper plant
crowd_press: thousands marched towards Collectorate on 22 May 2018 (Deccan Herald)
state_response: Police firing; Section 144; Justice Aruna Jagadeesan Commission (report found firing unprovoked, action against 17 police); Madras HC ordered CBI probe
outcome: TN government ordered permanent closure of plant on 28 May 2018; plant remained shut

name: SSC CGL paper-leak protests
city_or_district: CGO Complex, Lodhi Road, New Delhi
trigger: Alleged leak/screen-sharing in SSC CGL Tier-II exam (17-21 Feb 2018)
organisers: Job aspirants; Yuva Halla Bol and student groups; politicians visited
demands: CBI inquiry; cancel and re-conduct exam; reform SSC
crowd_press: thousands outside SSC office (Careers360/Newslaundry)
state_response: SSC chairman offered SIT; Home Minister Rajnath Singh announced CBI inquiry on 5 Mar 2018
outcome: CBI probe ordered; protest ended; CBI chargesheets later

name: Kisan Long March (Nashik to Mumbai)
trigger: Non-implementation of 2017 loan waiver, Forest Rights Act land titles for Adivasi cultivators, MSP
organisers: All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS, CPI-M)
demands: Unconditional loan waiver; FRA land titles; MSP at 1.5x comprehensive cost; river-linking; pensions
crowd_organiser: 25,000 at start rising to c. 50,000 at Mumbai (AIKS/PARI)
crowd_press: 30,000-40,000 (Business Today; Al Jazeera)
state_response: Fadnavis government met delegation and gave written assurance accepting most demands on 12 Mar 2018
outcome: March called off with written assurances; AIKS declared victory; follow-up march Feb 2019 called off after fresh assurances

name: Anna Hazare's Lokpal and farmers' hunger strike
trigger: Non-appointment of Lokpal four years after Act; Swaminathan Commission recommendations unimplemented
organisers: Anna Hazare and supporters (Bhrashtachar Virodhi Jan Andolan)
demands: Appoint Lokpal and Lokayuktas; implement Swaminathan report on MSP; electoral reforms
crowd_press: around 3,000 on day one, thinning thereafter (The Print/HT)
state_response: Maharashtra CM Fadnavis and MoS Gajendra Shekhawat conveyed Centre's written assurances on Lokpal and farmer demands
outcome: Fast ended on seventh day (29 Mar 2018); Lokpal eventually appointed Mar 2019

name: Bharat Bandh against dilution of SC/ST Act
state: Nationwide (MP, Rajasthan, UP, Bihar, Punjab, Odisha, Delhi)
city_or_district: Gwalior; Morena; Bhind; Alwar; Meerut; Patna
trigger: Supreme Court judgment of 20 Mar 2018 barring automatic arrest and allowing anticipatory bail under SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
organisers: Dalit and Adivasi organisations (Bhim Army, NACDOR, SC/ST associations) backed by opposition parties
demands: Restore original SC/ST Act provisions; review of SC order
state_response: Curfew in Morena, Gwalior, Bhind; Centre filed review petition in SC same day; hundreds detained
outcome: Parliament passed SC/ST (PoA) Amendment Act in Aug 2018 restoring provisions; >100 trains disrupted

name: Kathua and Unnao rape protests
state: Nationwide (Delhi; Jammu and Kashmir; Uttar Pradesh; Punjab)
city_or_district: India Gate, New Delhi; Jammu; Kathua; Lucknow
trigger: Chargesheet in Kathua rape-murder of 8-year-old (9 Apr) and Unnao survivor's suicide attempt outside UP CM's residence (8 Apr) implicating BJP MLA Kuldeep Sengar
organisers: Civil society and student groups; Congress (midnight candlelight march 12 Apr led by Rahul Gandhi); lawyers' groups
demands: Justice for victims; arrest of MLA Sengar; action against lawyers obstructing Kathua chargesheet
crowd_press: hundreds at India Gate; 500+ at local marches (Tribune)
state_response: CBI arrested Sengar 13 Apr 2018; Supreme Court moved Kathua trial to Pathankot; Criminal Law (Amendment) Ordinance 21 Apr 2018 introduced death penalty for child rape
outcome: Ordinance/POCSO amendment; convictions in Kathua (June 2019) and Unnao (Dec 2019) cases

name: Bharat Bandh against fuel price hike
city_or_district: Delhi; Patna; Jehanabad; Mumbai; Bengaluru; Kerala; Odisha
trigger: Record petrol (Rs 80.73) and diesel (Rs 72.83) prices in Delhi; rupee depreciation
organisers: Congress with 21 opposition parties; Left parties
demands: Cut excise duty; bring fuel under GST
violence: clashes (vehicles damaged and tyres burnt in Patna; roads blocked in Bihar, Odisha)
deaths: n/a (two-year-old girl died when ambulance stuck in Jehanabad blockade; officials disputed link)
state_response: Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan cut state VAT; Centre refused excise cut
outcome: Mixed response; no central relief; partial state VAT cuts
election_within_6_months: yes: Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Telangana assembly Nov-Dec 2018

name: Sabarimala women-entry protests
city_or_district: Pathanamthitta (Nilakkal, Pamba, Sannidhanam); Thiruvananthapuram; statewide hartals
trigger: Supreme Court 4:1 verdict (28 Sep 2018) lifting ban on women aged 10-50 entering Sabarimala; entry of two women on 2 Jan 2019
organisers: Sabarimala Karma Samithi; BJP; Nair Service Society; RSS-linked groups (counter: LDF Women's Wall 1 Jan 2019)
demands: Review/overturn of verdict; protect temple custom
crowd_press: thousands took part in protests across Kerala (The News Minute, Oct 2018)
deaths: 1 (protester hit by stones at Pandalam, 3 Jan 2019; a second death indirectly attributed to hartal)
state_response: Section 144 at Nilakkal/Pamba; thousands of arrests; police escorted women devotees; LDF government backed verdict
outcome: Two women entered 2 Jan 2019; statewide hartal 3 Jan with 20+ CPI(M) offices attacked; SC referred review to larger bench Nov 2019

name: Kisan Mukti March (Delhi)
city_or_district: Ramlila Maidan to Parliament Street, New Delhi
trigger: Agrarian distress, debt and prices; AIKSCC call for special session of Parliament on farm crisis
organisers: All India Kisan Sangharsh Coordination Committee (200+ farm organisations)
demands: Three-week special Parliament session; two private bills on debt freedom and guaranteed MSP (C2+50%)
state_response: Police permitted march to Parliament Street; opposition leaders addressed rally
outcome: No special session; bills not taken up; built coalition later central to 2020-21 protest
election_within_6_months: yes: Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Mizoram assembly Nov-Dec 2018; Lok Sabha Apr-May 2019

name: Two-day nationwide general strike 2019
trigger: Labour code bills, privatisation, unemployment and minimum wage; 'anti-worker policies'
organisers: Joint platform of 10 central trade unions (INTUC, AITUC, HMS, CITU, AIUTUC, TUCC, SEWA, AICCTU, LPF, UTUC); BMS stayed away; farmer and teacher unions joined
demands: 12-point charter: statutory minimum wage, no labour-law dilution, halt privatisation/FDI in PSUs, universal social security, end contractualisation, price control; withdraw labour codes
violence: clashes (CPI(M)-TMC scuffle in Asansol; bus vandalism in West Bengal)
state_response: West Bengal government ran transport and warned staff; arrests of picketers
outcome: No concessions; Code on Wages passed later in 2019

name: Mamata Banerjee's 'Save the Constitution' dharna
trigger: CBI team attempted to question Kolkata Police Commissioner Rajeev Kumar in Saradha chit-fund case on 3 Feb 2019; CBI officers detained by Kolkata Police
organisers: Trinamool Congress (CM Mamata Banerjee with ministers and opposition leaders in solidarity)
demands: Stop 'misuse' of CBI; protect federalism and Constitution
state_response: Centre-state standoff; CBI moved Supreme Court, which barred coercive action against Kumar but directed him to appear in Shillong
outcome: Dharna ended 5 Feb 2019 after SC order; TMC claimed 'moral victory'

name: Gujjar reservation agitation (Malarna Dungar rail blockade)
city_or_district: Malarna Dungar, Sawai Madhopur; Dholpur; Karauli
trigger: Demand for 5% separate quota for Gujjars and four other MBC communities after earlier 2008-2015 agitations and court hurdles
organisers: Gujjar Aarakshan Sangharsh Samiti (Col. Kirori Singh Bainsla)
demands: 5% reservation for Gujjar, Raika-Rebari, Gadia Luhar, Banjara, Gadaria in jobs and education
violence: clashes (police tear gas on protesters in Dholpur; rail and highway blockades)
state_response: Rajasthan assembly passed 5% MBC quota bill 13 Feb 2019; minister handed draft to Bainsla on the tracks
outcome: Agitation called off after eight days on written assurance; 64+148 trains cancelled across two railway zones

name: Kashmir protests and lockdown after revocation of Article 370
trigger: Abrogation of Article 370 and bifurcation of J&K into Union Territories (5 Aug 2019) under communications blackout and mass detention
organisers: Largely spontaneous (Soura, Anchar); mainstream and separatist leaders detained
demands: Restore special status and statehood; release detainees; restore communications
crowd_press: more than 10,000 at Soura, Srinagar on 9 Aug 2019 (Al Jazeera, citing police/local sources)
violence: clashes (tear gas, pellet guns and live rounds in the air at Soura; at least 152 treated for pellet/tear-gas injuries 5-21 Aug at two Srinagar hospitals)
deaths: 1 (teenager died of pellet and tear-gas shell wounds, Sept 2019, per Al Jazeera); official claims of zero deaths disputed
internet_shutdown: yes: entire Kashmir Valley (landline, mobile and internet blackout from 4-5 Aug 2019; broadband/2G restored in stages from Jan 2020)
state_response: Communications blackout; movement restrictions; thousands detained incl. three former CMs; Home Minister's 'no bullet, no tear gas' claim contradicted by hospital records
outcome: Street protests contained by Sept 2019; restrictions eased gradually; SC Anuradha Bhasin judgment (Jan 2020) on internet shutdowns

name: Aarey forest tree-felling protests
trigger: Bombay HC (4 Oct 2019) refused to declare Aarey a forest; MMRCL began felling c. 2,600 trees overnight for Metro-3 car shed
organisers: Save Aarey movement; environmental activists and residents; Shiv Sena youth wing
demands: Stop felling; relocate car shed; declare Aarey a forest
violence: clashes (protesters tried to stop felling; 29 arrested for obstructing/assaulting police)
state_response: Section 144 imposed in Aarey, entry points sealed; 29 arrested and bailed; SC special bench stayed further felling 7 Oct 2019
outcome: Trees already cut (state claimed 98% of plan); car shed later shifted to Kanjurmarg by MVA govt (2020) and back to Aarey by Shinde govt (2022)

name: TSRTC employees' strike
trigger: Failure of talks over demand to merge Telangana State Road Transport Corporation with government; c. 48,000-50,000 employees struck from 5 Oct 2019
organisers: TSRTC Joint Action Committee of employee unions
demands: Merger of TSRTC with state government; pay revision; recruitment; against privatisation of routes
crowd_press: nearly 50,000 employees on strike (Gulf News/PTI)
violence: none (several employee suicides/deaths reported during strike)
state_response: CM KCR declared striking employees 'self-dismissed'; temporary drivers hired; proposal to privatise 5,100 routes; HC hearings
outcome: Strike called off after 51-52 days on 25 Nov 2019; government later took employees back (Nov 28) without merger

name: JNU hostel fee hike protests
city_or_district: Jawaharlal Nehru University; march to Parliament (18 Nov); Rashtrapati Bhavan march (9 Dec)
trigger: Draft hostel manual raising hostel fees (by up to c. 1000%) and imposing dress code and curfew
organisers: JNU Students' Union (Left-led); JNUTA support; ABVP separate protests
demands: Complete rollback of fee hike and new hostel manual
crowd_press: thousands marched towards Parliament on 18 Nov 2019 (Gulf News/AFP)
violence: clashes (lathicharge and detentions 18 Nov and 9 Dec 2019; metro stations closed)
state_response: MHRD three-member mediation committee; partial rollback (service/utility charges) for BPL students; police lathicharge on marches
outcome: Partial rollback; students continued boycott; 5 Jan 2020 masked-mob attack on campus followed

name: Hyderabad veterinarian (Disha) rape-murder protests
trigger: Gang-rape and murder of a 26-year-old veterinary doctor near Shamshabad on 27 Nov 2019; burnt body found at Shadnagar on 28 Nov; four arrested
organisers: Spontaneous public protests; women's groups; students
demands: Swift justice; death penalty; police accountability
crowd_press: hundreds outside Shadnagar police station on 30 Nov 2019 (Euronews/Reuters)
violence: clashes (crowd demanded accused be handed over; slippers hurled; police lathicharge to shift accused)
state_response: Fast-track court announced; accused moved to Cherlapally jail; all four shot dead by police at crime-scene 'reconstruction' on 6 Dec 2019; SC-appointed Sirpurkar commission (2022) found encounter staged
outcome: Protests ended after the encounter, which drew public celebration and rights criticism

name: Assam anti-CAA agitation
trigger: Passage of Citizenship (Amendment) Bill in Lok Sabha (9 Dec) and Rajya Sabha (11 Dec 2019); fear of demographic change and dilution of Assam Accord
organisers: All Assam Students' Union (AASU); Krishak Mukti Sangram Samiti (Akhil Gogoi); artists and civil society
demands: Withdraw CAA from Assam; implement Assam Accord Clause 6
deaths: 5 (4 shot in Guwahati firing; 5th in subsequent firing)
internet_shutdown: yes: Guwahati from 11 Dec 2019, extended to whole of Assam on 12 Dec; lifted c. 20 Dec
state_response: Indefinite curfew in Guwahati; Army deployed; 1,026 arrested in 12 days; Akhil Gogoi arrested (NIA/UAPA); 25 firing incidents, 19 lathicharges (govt data)
outcome: Curfew eased 17 Dec; protests continued peacefully for months; spawned regional parties (AJP, Raijor Dal)

name: Aligarh Muslim University anti-CAA protest and police action
trigger: CAA passage (12 Dec protests); solidarity with Jamia students on evening of 15 Dec; VC called in police
organisers: AMU Students' Union; AMU Teachers' Association (silent march)
demands: Repeal CAA; action against police excesses
violence: clashes (police with batons, tear gas, pellets; stun grenades reported)
internet_shutdown: yes: Aligarh (internet suspended from 15 Dec 2019; see Quint timeline)
state_response: VC admitted calling police; campus vacated and winter break advanced; FIRs and arrests of students
outcome: Students resumed peaceful protest on campus late Dec; NHRC notice; crowd-funding for injured

name: Jamia Millia Islamia anti-CAA protest and police action
city_or_district: Jamia Nagar; New Friends Colony; Mathura Road
trigger: CAA passage; student march towards Parliament blocked; buses burnt near New Friends Colony on 15 Dec; police entered campus and library
organisers: Jamia students and Jamia Coordination Committee; local residents
demands: Repeal CAA/NRC; action against police for campus entry
crowd_press: several thousand students and non-students marching on 15 Dec (Scholars at Risk)
state_response: Police entered campus at 6:46 pm without permission, used batons and tear gas; c. 100 detained and released 3:30 am; 60-80 injured
outcome: Nationwide campus solidarity protests; NHRC inquiry; Delhi HC petitions; sit-in continued at Gate 7 into 2020

name: Shaheen Bagh anti-CAA sit-in
trigger: Citizenship (Amendment) Act 2019 and police action at Jamia Millia Islamia on 15 Dec 2019
organisers: Local women residents (leaderless)
demands: Repeal CAA; stop NRC and NPR
violence: none (a gunman fired shots near site on 1 Feb 2020 without casualties)
state_response: Supreme Court appointed interlocutors (Feb 2020); Oct 2020 SC ruling against indefinite occupation of public roads
outcome: Sit-in of 101 days cleared on 24 Mar 2020 under COVID-19 lockdown; became model for women-led sit-ins nationwide

name: Amaravati capital farmers' protest
city_or_district: Amaravati (29 villages, Guntur); Maha Padayatra Amaravati-Tirupati (Nov-Dec 2021)
trigger: CM Jagan Mohan Reddy announced three capitals (Amaravati legislative, Visakhapatnam executive, Kurnool judicial) on 18 Dec 2019 after farmers of 29 villages had pooled c. 33,000 acres for Amaravati
organisers: Amaravati Parirakshana Samithi / Amaravati Joint Action Committee; farmers and women of 29 capital villages; NRI supporters
demands: Retain Amaravati as sole capital; honour land-pooling agreements
violence: clashes (protesters complained of police action; lathicharge and detentions Dec 2019)
state_response: Section 144 and detentions; AP Decentralisation Act 2020 later withdrawn (Nov 2021); AP High Court verdict 3 Mar 2022 directed capital development at Amaravati
outcome: Protest crossed 1,000 days on 17 Dec 2022 with second Maha Padayatra (Amaravati-Arasavalli); first 400 km padayatra to Tirupati in late 2021; protest finally ended after 1,631 days in June 2024

name: Mangaluru anti-CAA protest and police firing
trigger: Nationwide anti-CAA protest day 19 Dec 2019; crowd gathered near Bunder police station despite Section 144
organisers: Local Muslim youth and organisations; opposition parties
demands: Repeal CAA/NRC
crowd_press: around 2,000 gathered at Bunder, 4.15-5.30 pm (Deccan Herald citing police)
deaths: 2 (Jaleel Kudroli, 49, and Nausheen, 23, shot by police)
internet_shutdown: yes: Mangaluru city and Dakshina Kannada district (48 hours from 10 pm 19 Dec 2019)
state_response: Curfew till 21 Dec; police claimed self-defence to protect police station; firing victims named in FIR; magisterial/CID inquiry
outcome: Ex-gratia announced then withheld pending probe; normalcy by 22 Dec

name: Uttar Pradesh anti-CAA protests
city_or_district: Lucknow; Kanpur; Meerut; Firozabad; Bijnor; Varanasi; Muzaffarnagar
trigger: CAA passage and police action at Jamia/AMU; statewide protests on 19-20 Dec 2019
organisers: Local Muslim organisations; civil society (Lucknow); Samajwadi Party and Congress workers
demands: Repeal CAA/NRC
deaths: 16-17 by 22 Dec (Tribune tally; later counts up to 23); nine killed on 20 Dec alone (HT)
internet_shutdown: yes: 16 UP districts incl. Lucknow, Meerut, Kanpur, Bijnor, Aligarh (19-23 Dec 2019)
state_response: Section 144 statewide; 879 arrested and 5,312 preventively detained (UP Police); property-seizure notices to protesters in Lucknow on CM's orders (later quashed by SC 2022); internet shutdowns
outcome: Protests suppressed within days; Priyanka Gandhi visited Bijnor victims' families; NHRC and HC scrutiny of police firing

name: Nationwide general strike (Bharat Bandh) January 2020
trigger: Labour codes, bank mergers, corporatisation of ordnance factories; unions also opposed CAA/NPR; talks with labour minister failed 2 Jan
organisers: Joint platform of 10 central trade unions (INTUC, AITUC, HMS, CITU, AIUTUC, TUCC, SEWA, AICCTU, LPF, UTUC); BMS stayed away; student groups and farmers' organisations joined
demands: 12-point charter: statutory minimum wage, no labour-law dilution, halt privatisation/FDI in PSUs, universal social security, end contractualisation, price control; withdraw labour codes; oppose CAA/NPR; 14-point charter
state_response: Government talks failed; West Bengal and other states deployed police to keep transport running
outcome: No concessions; three labour codes passed Sept 2020

name: North-east Delhi riots
city_or_district: Jaffrabad; Maujpur; Shiv Vihar; Khajuri Khas; Mustafabad
trigger: Women's anti-CAA sit-in blocking Jaffrabad road; BJP leader Kapil Mishra's 'ultimatum' rally at Maujpur on 23 Feb; clashes escalated into communal violence
organisers: n/a (pro- and anti-CAA mobs; no formal organiser)
state_response: Delhi Police and paramilitary deployment after delay; Section 144; UAPA conspiracy case against activists (Umar Khalid, others); c. 750 FIRs
outcome: 53 dead (around a dozen Hindus), 200+ injured, homes, shops and mosques burnt; trials ongoing
election_within_6_months: yes: Delhi assembly 8 Feb 2020 (two weeks earlier)

name: Migrant workers' lockdown protests
city_or_district: Anand Vihar, Delhi (28-29 Mar); Bandra, Mumbai (14 Apr); Surat (Apr-May)
trigger: Nationwide COVID-19 lockdown from 24 Mar 2020 left migrant workers without wages, food or transport; extension announced 14 Apr
organisers: Spontaneous gatherings of stranded workers
demands: Transport to home states; wages and food; lifting of travel restrictions
crowd_press: thousands at Anand Vihar 28-29 Mar; c. 1,000 at Bandra 14 Apr 2020 (Business Today; Statesman)
violence: clashes (lathicharge at Bandra; stone-pelting in Surat)
state_response: Lathicharge and FIRs; Shramik Special trains from 1 May 2020; state buses; Supreme Court orders on transport and wages (June 2020)
outcome: Shramik Specials moved several million workers; policy focus on migrant registration and ration portability
election_within_6_months: yes: Bihar assembly 28 Oct-7 Nov 2020 (within 6 months of end; major origin state)

name: Farmers' protest against three farm laws
state: Punjab; Haryana; Uttar Pradesh; Delhi borders (national)
city_or_district: Singhu; Tikri; Ghazipur; Shahjahanpur; Punjab rail roko sites
trigger: Three farm ordinances (June 2020) and Acts (Sept 2020) liberalising agri-marketing, contract farming and essential commodities
organisers: Samyukt Kisan Morcha (c. 40 unions incl. BKU Ugrahan, BKU Rajewal, BKU Tikait, KMSC); AIKSCC
demands: Repeal three farm laws; legal guarantee of MSP; withdraw Electricity Amendment Bill; scrap stubble-burning penalties
crowd_organiser: lakhs at borders (SKM); c. 50,000 women at Singhu/Tikri on 8 Mar 2021 (Down To Earth)
crowd_press: tens of thousands camped at Delhi borders (House of Commons Library)
violence: clashes (26 Jan 2021 Republic Day tractor rally, Red Fort; water cannons/tear gas Nov 2020)
deaths: n/a official; SKM claimed c. 700 protester deaths over the year (Wikipedia tally 789)
internet_shutdown: yes: Singhu, Tikri, Ghazipur and Haryana districts, 26 Jan-early Feb 2021 (MHA/Haryana orders)
state_response: 11 rounds of talks; SC stayed laws Jan 2021 and formed committee; barricades, trenches, nails at borders; FIRs after 26 Jan
outcome: PM announced repeal 19 Nov 2021; Farm Laws Repeal Act 29 Nov 2021; protest ended 11 Dec 2021 with MSP committee and case-withdrawal assurances
election_within_6_months: yes: Bihar assembly Oct-Nov 2020; WB/Assam/Kerala/TN Mar-Apr 2021; Punjab and UP assembly Feb-Mar 2022 (within 6 months of end)

name: DJ Halli-KG Halli violence (Bengaluru)
city_or_district: DJ Halli, KG Halli, Kaval Byrasandra, Bengaluru
trigger: Allegedly derogatory Facebook post about the Prophet by Naveen, a relative of Congress MLA Akhanda Srinivas Murthy; crowd gathered at KG Halli police station demanding arrest
organisers: n/a (spontaneous mob; Karnataka cabinet-accepted magisterial report alleged SDPI role)
demands: Arrest of the accused
state_response: Police firing; Section 144 till 18 Aug; 100+ then 60 more arrested; NIA took over; magisterial inquiry; HC called it act of terror
outcome: MLA's house and police station attacked and vehicles torched; property-damage recovery claims; trials ongoing

name: Punjab farmers' rail roko against farm laws
trigger: Passage of three farm bills in Parliament (17-20 Sep 2020); KMSC began squatting on tracks 24 Sep; 30 unions extended indefinite rail roko from 1 Oct
organisers: Kisan Mazdoor Sangharsh Committee; 30-31 Punjab farm unions (BKU Ugrahan, BKU Rajewal and others)
demands: Repeal three farm laws; legal MSP
state_response: Railways suspended passenger and then goods trains to Punjab for c. 2 months; Punjab assembly passed counter-bills (Oct 2020); CM Amarinder appealed for relaxation
outcome: Unions cleared tracks 23 Nov 2020 ahead of Delhi Chalo; Railways resumed trains; protest shifted to Delhi borders

name: Hathras gang-rape protests
city_or_district: Hathras (Boolgarhi); Jantar Mantar, New Delhi; Lucknow
trigger: Death (29 Sep) of 19-year-old Dalit woman gang-raped on 14 Sep 2020 and her forced night-time cremation by police without family
organisers: Bhim Army; Congress; AAP; student and women's groups; civil society
demands: Justice and CBI probe; action against police and district officials; protection for family
crowd_press: hundreds at Jantar Mantar on 2 Oct 2020 (Tribune)
violence: none (police detained/manhandled opposition leaders; village sealed)
state_response: Village sealed and media barred; SIT; CBI probe ordered 10 Oct; FIRs for 'conspiracy'; journalist Siddique Kappan arrested under UAPA
outcome: CBI chargesheet Dec 2020 against four accused; Allahabad HC suo motu hearings on cremation

name: Nationwide general strike November 2020 (with farmers' Delhi Chalo)
city_or_district: Kerala; West Bengal; Punjab; Haryana; Delhi borders
trigger: Four labour codes passed Sept 2020; three farm laws; privatisation during pandemic
organisers: Joint platform of 10 central trade unions (INTUC, AITUC, HMS, CITU, AIUTUC, TUCC, SEWA, AICCTU, LPF, UTUC); BMS stayed away; supported by AIKSCC/SKM farmer organisations
demands: 12-point charter: statutory minimum wage, no labour-law dilution, halt privatisation/FDI in PSUs, universal social security, end contractualisation, price control; scrap four labour codes and three farm laws; minimum wage Rs 26,000; MSP at C2+50%
violence: clashes (water cannon and tear gas on farmers at Haryana-Delhi borders same day)
state_response: Postal, banking, insurance, mining affected; farmers allowed into Delhi borders after clashes
outcome: No concessions on codes; coincided with start of year-long farmers' protest
election_within_6_months: yes: West Bengal, Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry assembly Mar-Apr 2021

name: Visakhapatnam Steel Plant anti-privatisation protest
trigger: Cabinet (CCEA) approval on 27 Jan 2021 of 100% strategic disinvestment of Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Ltd (Vizag Steel); relay hunger strike began at Kurmannapalem junction 12 Feb 2021
organisers: Visakha Ukku Parirakshana Porata Committee (VUPPC, joint trade unions); supported by all AP parties
demands: Withdraw 100% strategic sale; allot captive iron-ore mines; retain public-sector status
violence: none (bandh observed peacefully; later sieges of plant office)
state_response: AP CM assured assembly resolution against privatisation (Feb 2021); Centre maintained disinvestment decision
outcome: Relay hunger strike crossed 500 days in mid-2022 and continued; privatisation not completed by end-2022

name: West Bengal post-poll violence protests
city_or_district: Kolkata; Cooch Behar; Nandigram; Birbhum; Howrah
trigger: Violence between TMC and BJP supporters after 2 May 2021 assembly results; BJP 'dharna' and nationwide protest call (5 May)
organisers: BJP and TMC cadres; Bengal BJP state leadership
demands: Protection of party workers; central intervention; CBI probe
deaths: 11-14 (press tallies for May 2021; NHRC panel recorded 29 murder complaints 2 May-20 Jun; police did not confirm)
state_response: Calcutta HC-appointed NHRC committee (report July 2021: 1,934 complaints incl. 29 murder, 12 rape/sexual assault, 940 loot/arson); HC ordered CBI probe into murders and rapes and SIT for other cases (Aug 2021)
outcome: CBI chargesheets; violence tapered by June 2021; BJP held nationwide protests on 5 May 2021
election_within_6_months: yes: West Bengal assembly Mar-Apr 2021 (immediately before)

name: Silger anti-CRPF-camp protest and police firing
trigger: CRPF camp set up overnight on 12 May 2021 at Silger without gram sabha consent (PESA); villagers gathered from 14 May; police fired on 17 May
organisers: Adivasi villagers of Silger and neighbouring villages; Moolvasi Bachao Manch
demands: Remove camp; inquiry into firing; compensation; respect PESA gram sabha consent
crowd_press: more than 10,000 villagers on 17 May 2021 (Caravan/fact-finding)
deaths: 3 (Kawasi Vaga, Ursam Bhima, Uika Pandu; a pregnant woman died later in stampede per some reports)
state_response: Police claimed Maoist firing; independent observers disputed; no judicial inquiry; protesters petitioned Governor
outcome: Sit-in continued for years at Silger; camp stayed

name: Ladakh statehood and Sixth Schedule movement
trigger: Ladakh made a Union Territory without legislature (Aug 2019); fears over land, jobs and cultural protection; LAB-KDA joint platform from 2021
organisers: Leh Apex Body (LAB); Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA); Sonam Wangchuk
demands: Statehood; Sixth Schedule inclusion; Ladakh Public Service Commission; two Lok Sabha seats; job and land reservation for locals
crowd_press: thousands mobilised in Leh and Kargil (Kashmir Life; Wikipedia)
state_response: MHA formed high-powered committee under MoS Nityanand Rai (Jan 2023); talks with LAB-KDA
outcome: Unresolved through 2022; movement escalated 2023-24 (Wangchuk fasts)

name: Haryana HSSC constable exam paper leak and aspirants' outcry
trigger: Solved answer key for HSSC male constable exam (7-8 Aug 2021) leaked and sold (one key for Rs 1 crore); exam cancelled on 7 Aug after Kaithal police arrests
organisers: Job aspirants; Congress (Randeep Surjewala demanded HC-monitored CBI probe)
demands: CBI probe; action on 'serial' paper leaks; fresh transparent exam
crowd_press: thousands of aspirants had sat the cancelled exam (Tribune); no protest crowd figure published
state_response: Exam cancelled; Kaithal police arrested 128 by 11 Aug (167 by 2025); leak traced to Jammu printing agency
outcome: Re-examination later held; opposition CBI demand not accepted

name: Darrang (Dholpur-Gorukhuti) eviction protests and police firing
trigger: Eviction drive clearing Bengali-origin Muslim settlers from c. 4,500 bighas for Gorukhuti agricultural project; residents resisted on 23 Sep 2021
organisers: Affected residents; AAMSU and opposition parties protested afterwards
demands: Halt evictions; rehabilitation; inquiry into firing
state_response: Judicial inquiry ordered under retired HC judge; photographer Bijoy Bania arrested for stomping on body; CID probe; evictions continued
outcome: Evictions completed; inquiry slow to start; opposition condemnation

name: Rajasthan REET paper-leak protests
trigger: REET teacher eligibility exam (26 Sep 2021) paper leaked two days earlier; SOG arrests exposed racket; alleged official involvement
organisers: Unemployed aspirants (Rajasthan Berozgar Ekikrit Mahasangh); BJP/BJYM; ABVP
demands: CBI probe; cancellation of exam; action against ministers and officials; fresh recruitment
crowd_press: hundreds of youths outside Rajasthan Assembly (Outlook, Feb 2022)
violence: clashes (water cannon and lathicharge on BJP and aspirants' marches in Jaipur)
internet_shutdown: no (mobile internet was suspended on exam day 26 Sep 2021 to prevent cheating, not for protests)
state_response: SOG probe; Board chairman D.P. Jaroli sacked and secretary suspended; REET Level-2 exam cancelled; anti-cheating law (2022)
outcome: Level-2 exam cancelled and re-held July 2022; no CBI probe granted

name: Lakhimpur Kheri violence (Tikunia)
trigger: Farmers protesting Deputy CM's visit were rammed by convoy including vehicle of Ashish Mishra, son of MoS Home Ajay Mishra; retaliatory lynching
organisers: Samyukt Kisan Morcha; BKU (Tikait); local farmers
demands: Arrest of Ashish Mishra; sacking of minister Ajay Mishra Teni; compensation and justice
state_response: Section 144; opposition leaders detained/stopped (Priyanka Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav); Rs 45 lakh compensation; SC-monitored SIT; Ashish Mishra arrested 9 Oct 2021
outcome: SIT chargesheet (Jan 2022) for murder/conspiracy; charges framed Dec 2022; SKM 'antim ardas' 12 Oct and rail roko 18 Oct

name: Tripura communal violence and VHP rallies
city_or_district: Panisagar and Dharmanagar (North Tripura); Udaipur; Agartala
trigger: VHP/Hindu Jagran Manch rallies (21 and 26 Oct 2021) protesting anti-Hindu violence in Bangladesh during Durga Puja; Chamtilla mosque and Muslim shops vandalised at Panisagar 26 Oct
organisers: Vishwa Hindu Parishad; Hindu Jagran Manch; Bajrang Dal (rallies); Muslim organisations (counter-protests, later Jamiat fact-finding)
demands: (VHP) action on Bangladesh violence; (Muslim groups) protection, arrests of vandals
internet_shutdown: no record in cited sources (internet suspended in later Tripura incidents, not confirmed for Oct 2021)
state_response: Section 144 in North Tripura; 102 arrested; UAPA FIRs against 102 social-media accounts, journalists and lawyers (SC later protected them)
outcome: Violence ended by 29 Oct; UAPA cases drew Editors Guild and SC criticism; follow-on protests in Maharashtra (Amravati) Nov 2021

name: MSRTC employees' strike
trigger: Demand to merge loss-making Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation with state government and give employees government-staff status; triggered by employee suicides
organisers: MSRTC employee unions and action committee; advocate Gunaratna Sadavarte
demands: Merger with government; pay parity; action on employee suicides
crowd_press: over 90,000 on MSRTC payroll; most struck (Deccan Herald/PTI)
violence: clashes (8 Apr 2022 stone-pelting and footwear hurled at Sharad Pawar's Mumbai residence; 110 arrested)
state_response: Government suspended/dismissed thousands; HC-appointed committee rejected merger; CM Uddhav Thackeray condemned Pawar-house attack; Sadavarte arrested
outcome: Strike ended Apr 2022 after HC urged return to work; merger denied, pay hike granted

name: Oting killings protests and anti-AFSPA movement (Nagaland)
city_or_district: Oting and Mon town (Mon district); Kohima; Dimapur
trigger: 21 Para Special Forces ambush killed six coal miners near Oting on 4 Dec 2021; seven more civilians and one soldier died in subsequent violence
organisers: Konyak Union; Eastern Nagaland People's Organisation; Naga Students' Federation; tribal hohos; church bodies
demands: Repeal AFSPA; prosecute soldiers responsible; justice and compensation
state_response: State SIT; Army Court of Inquiry; Nagaland assembly resolution demanding repeal (20 Dec); Hornbill Festival cancelled; MHA committee on AFSPA
outcome: AFSPA 'disturbed area' coverage reduced in Nagaland, Assam, Manipur from 1 Apr 2022; MoD denied sanction to prosecute 30 soldiers (2023); SC stayed proceedings

name: Manipur anti-AFSPA mobilisation after Oting killings
trigger: Oting killings in neighbouring Nagaland revived demand to repeal AFSPA in Manipur, long a target of Irom Sharmila's 16-year fast (2000-2016)
organisers: Civil society organisations; student bodies; Irom Sharmila (statements)
demands: Repeal of Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act from the North-East
state_response: Manipur government under N. Biren Singh did not join Nagaland/Meghalaya CMs' repeal demand at the time; AFSPA later withdrawn from 15 police-station areas (Apr 2022)
outcome: Partial reduction of AFSPA 'disturbed areas' in Manipur valley districts from 1 Apr 2022

name: Karnataka hijab row
trigger: Government PU College Udupi barred six hijab-wearing students from class (CDC resolution 1 Jan 2022); counter-protests by saffron-shawl students
organisers: Campus Front of India (students); counter: ABVP and Hindu groups
demands: Allow hijab in classrooms vs enforcement of uniform
violence: clashes (stone-pelting in Shivamogga and Davangere 8 Feb; stand-offs at colleges)
state_response: Government Order on uniforms (5 Feb); schools/colleges shut 3 days; Section 144 in Udupi, Bengaluru, Shivamogga and other districts; HC interim ban on religious dress
outcome: Karnataka High Court upheld hijab restriction 15 Mar 2022; Supreme Court split verdict 13 Oct 2022

name: RRB NTPC / Group D exam protests
city_or_district: Patna; Gaya; Ara; Nawada; Sitamarhi; Prayagraj
trigger: RRB NTPC CBT-1 results (15 Jan 2022) and decision to hold second-stage CBT for NTPC and Group D seen as 'cheating' aspirants

name: Two-day nationwide general strike March 2022

trigger: Labour codes, privatisation (banks, PSUs, National Monetisation Pipeline), rising prices, unemployment
organisers: Joint platform of 10 central trade unions (INTUC, AITUC, HMS, CITU, AIUTUC, TUCC, SEWA, AICCTU, LPF, UTUC); BMS stayed away; bank, insurance, coal, steel, postal unions gave strike notices
demands: 12-point charter: statutory minimum wage, no labour-law dilution, halt privatisation/FDI in PSUs, universal social security, end contractualisation, price control; scrap labour codes; halt privatisation and NMP; MGNREGA wage hike
state_response: Kerala High Court restrained government staff; ESMA-type warnings in some states; banking and transport hit in Left-ruled states
outcome: No concessions

name: Khargone Ram Navami violence and demolitions
trigger: Stone-pelting on Ram Navami procession passing Talab Chowk mosque at evening prayer time (10 Apr 2022); arson and clashes followed
organisers: n/a (procession by Hindu organisations; local Muslim residents; no formal protest organiser)
deaths: 1 (Ibrees Khan, killed during violence; body found days later)

outcome: Curfew lifted in stages; demolitions criticised as unlawful; court acquitted 11 accused in 2023 for lack of evidence

name: Jahangirpuri violence and demolition drive

organisers: n/a (Bajrang Dal procession; local Muslim residents; no formal protest organiser)
demands: n/a (post-violence: Muslim residents and opposition demanded halt to demolitions)
deaths: 0 (press reports of 9 injured incl. 8 police; Wikipedia lists one IB officer death, not corroborated in cited news)

outcome: c. 20 shops and mosque frontage demolished before SC stay; SC extended stay; PUDR fact-finding report

name: Protests over Nupur Sharma's remarks on the Prophet
state: Uttar Pradesh; Jharkhand; West Bengal; Delhi
city_or_district: Kanpur (3 Jun); Prayagraj; Saharanpur; Ranchi; Howrah; Jama Masjid Delhi
trigger: Remarks on the Prophet by BJP spokesperson Nupur Sharma (TV debate, 26 May) and Naveen Jindal; Gulf diplomatic backlash
organisers: Largely unorganised post-Friday-prayer gatherings; local Muslim organisations
demands: Arrest of Nupur Sharma and Naveen Jindal
internet_shutdown: yes: Ranchi (curfew and internet suspended); Howrah district (internet suspended)
state_response: 136 arrested across six UP districts; curfew in Ranchi; demolition of activist Javed Mohammad's house in Prayagraj (12 June)
outcome: BJP suspended Sharma (5 June); Supreme Court rebuked Sharma (July); follow-on Udaipur killing 28 June

name: Agnipath recruitment scheme protests
state: Bihar; Uttar Pradesh; Telangana; Haryana; Rajasthan; Madhya Pradesh; West Bengal
city_or_district: Patna; Lakhisarai; Samastipur; Ara; Secunderabad; Ballia; Palwal
trigger: Announcement of Agnipath four-year contractual military recruitment scheme on 14 June 2022 after two years without regular Army recruitment
organisers: Army aspirants and coaching centres; student organisations; opposition 'Bharat bandh' call for 20 June
demands: Withdraw Agnipath; restore regular recruitment; age relaxation for aspirants who lost years to COVID
state_response: One-time age ceiling raised to 23 for 2022; 10% reservation in CAPFs/Coast Guard for Agniveers; FIRs and arrests; 2,132 trains cancelled 15-23 June
outcome: Scheme implemented with concessions; trains torched in Bihar (Vikramshila, Sampark Kranti) and Secunderabad station vandalised

name: Vizhinjam port protest by fishing communities
trigger: Coastal erosion and loss of livelihood attributed to Adani Vizhinjam International Seaport construction (since Dec 2015); demand for impact study
organisers: Latin Catholic Archdiocese of Thiruvananthapuram; Janakeeya Padana Samithi; fisherfolk (c. 56,000 community)
demands: Seven-point charter: halt construction pending study; rehabilitation; compensation for coastal erosion; fuel subsidy; housing
violence: clashes (27 Nov 2022 attack on Vizhinjam police station; 29 police injured; cases against c. 3,000)
state_response: Kerala govt talks and partial concessions; HC orders to allow construction; cases against protesters incl. priests; Adani moved HC; FCRA freeze on church later
outcome: Protest called off after 138-140 days on 6 Dec 2022 after talks; construction resumed

name: Wrestlers' protest against WFI chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh
trigger: Sexual-harassment complaints by women wrestlers against Wrestling Federation of India president and BJP MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh; perceived inaction on FIRs
organisers: Olympic/Asian Games medallists Vinesh Phogat, Sakshi Malik, Bajrang Punia, Sangeeta Phogat; supported by farm unions and khap panchayats
demands: Arrest of Brij Bhushan; his removal from WFI; fair investigation
state_response: Delhi Police detained Phogat, Malik, Punia on 28 May 2023 as they tried to march to the new Parliament for a women's mahapanchayat; 35-day protest site cleared and tents removed; Haryana police blocked supporters from reaching Delhi
outcome: Protest site dismantled; wrestlers released same day; wrestlers later rejoined Railways duties; end_date is the day the site was cleared
election_within_6_months: yes: Karnataka assembly 2023-05-10; Mizoram 2023-11-07, Chhattisgarh 2023-11-07/17, Madhya Pradesh 2023-11-17, Rajasthan 2023-11-25, Telangana 2023-11-30

name: Manipur ethnic violence: ATSUM Tribal Solidarity March and outbreak phase
trigger: All Tribal Students' Union Manipur (ATSUM) 'Tribal Solidarity March' in all hill districts against Manipur High Court direction on Scheduled Tribe status for Meiteis; clashes erupted at Torbung, Churachandpur
organisers: ATSUM (march); subsequent violence between Kuki-Zo and Meitei groups
demands: Oppose ST status for Meiteis (ATSUM); later Kuki-Zo demand for separate administration
crowd_press: 15,000-20,000 at Churachandpur rally (India Today NE)
internet_shutdown: yes: statewide Manipur mobile internet shutdown from 3 May 2023 (widely reported; not detailed in cited URLs)
state_response: Curfew, shoot-at-sight orders, Army and Assam Rifles deployed; Army evacuated ~9,000 people (Deccan Herald); ~80 injured at Churachandpur hospital on day one
outcome: Prolonged ethnic conflict continuing into 2026; later phases in separate rows

name: Nuh (Mewat) communal violence during VHP Brajmandal Yatra
trigger: Attack on VHP/Bajrang Dal Brajmandal Jal Abhishek Yatra on 31 July 2023; preceded by viral video of cow vigilante Monu Manesar announcing participation
organisers: Vishva Hindu Parishad (yatra); local mobs (clashes)
deaths: 6-7 (incl. two home guards and a cleric)
internet_shutdown: yes: Nuh, Palwal, Faridabad till 2 Aug 2023; suspended again for re-run yatra on 28 Aug 2023
state_response: Curfew, Section 144, mobile internet and bulk SMS suspended, arrests; heavy security for re-run of yatra on 28 Aug 2023
outcome: Yatra re-held peacefully on 28 Aug 2023 under heavy security; 200+ injured in July violence
election_within_6_months: yes: Mizoram 2023-11-07, Chhattisgarh 2023-11-07/17, Madhya Pradesh 2023-11-17, Rajasthan 2023-11-25, Telangana 2023-11-30

name: Maratha reservation: Manoj Jarange's first hunger strike and Antarwali Sarati lathicharge
trigger: Demand for Kunbi (OBC) caste certificates for Marathas of Marathwada; police attempt to shift fasting Jarange to hospital
organisers: Manoj Jarange (Shivba Sanghatana); Maratha Kranti Morcha outfits
demands: Kunbi certificates for all Marathas; OBC reservation; dismissal of police officers responsible for lathicharge
state_response: Police lathicharge and tear gas on 1 Sep 2023; reports of firing, head injuries; politicians rushed to village; Bombay HC told govt to prevent law-and-order disturbance
outcome: Lathicharge made Jarange the face of the movement; Maratha outfits demanded Ajit Pawar quit govt; Jarange's fast continued ~2 weeks (end_date = lathicharge date); agitation recurred through 2026 (see later rows)
election_within_6_months: yes: Mizoram 2023-11-07, Chhattisgarh 2023-11-07/17, Madhya Pradesh 2023-11-17, Rajasthan 2023-11-25, Telangana 2023-11-30

name: Kurmi rail-roko agitation for Scheduled Tribe status (2023)
city_or_district: Muri, Gomoh, Chandil, Parasnath (Jharkhand); Paschim Medinipur, Purulia (WB)
trigger: Long-pending demand for ST status for Kurmis and Eighth Schedule inclusion of Kurmali
organisers: Kurmi caste organisations (Adivasi Kurmi Samaj and allied bodies)
demands: ST status for Kurmis; Kurmali language in Eighth Schedule
crowd_press: n/a (blockade announced at ~100 stations)
state_response: Railways cancelled/diverted trains; Calcutta High Court banned the agitation in West Bengal; police on alert

election_within_6_months: yes: Mizoram 2023-11-07, Chhattisgarh 2023-11-07/17, Madhya Pradesh 2023-11-17, Rajasthan 2023-11-25, Telangana 2023-11-30

name: Manipur: Imphal student protests over killing of two Meitei students
city_or_district: Imphal (Raj Bhavan, CM bungalow, Khwairamband area)
trigger: Viral photos (after internet restoration) showing two students missing since 6 July 2023, Phijam Hemjit (20) and Hijam Linthoingambi (17), dead in presence of armed men
organisers: School and college students (TG, Johnstone, Ibotonsana, CC Higher Secondary schools); student bodies
demands: Arrest of killers; accountability of state and central forces; justice for the two students
crowd_press: 'thousands' of students (India Today NE, Qrius)
internet_shutdown: yes: mobile internet ban re-imposed statewide after protests (had been restored days earlier)
state_response: Tear gas, baton charge and RAF deployment; 45 students injured on 26 Sept; schools closed till Friday; CBI took over the case (widely reported)
outcome: Protests continued for days; internet shutdown extended; CBI arrests in Oct 2023 (widely reported)
election_within_6_months: yes: Mizoram 2023-11-07, Chhattisgarh 2023-11-07/17, Madhya Pradesh 2023-11-17, Rajasthan 2023-11-25, Telangana 2023-11-30

name: Truckers' strike against BNS hit-and-run provision
state: Nationwide (Maharashtra, MP, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab most affected)
trigger: Section 106(2) Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita prescribing up to 10 years' jail for hit-and-run drivers who flee
organisers: All India Motor Transport Congress (AIMTC) and largely spontaneous driver walkouts
demands: Withdraw/review Section 106(2) BNS
state_response: Union Home Secretary met AIMTC on 2 Jan 2024; MHA assured provision would be invoked only after consultation
outcome: Strike called off night of 2 Jan 2024; Section 106(2) kept in abeyance and not notified into force; fuel-shortage panic in several cities
election_within_6_months: yes: Lok Sabha 2024-04-19 to 2024-06-01 (results 2024-06-04); Andhra Pradesh 2024-05-13; Odisha May-June 2024

name: Sandeshkhali women's protests against TMC strongman Shahjahan Sheikh
trigger: Attack on ED team raiding Shahjahan Sheikh on 5 Jan 2024; women alleged land-grab and sexual assault by Sheikh and aides Shibu Hazra and Uttam Sardar
organisers: Local women and villagers; BJP, CPI(M) mobilised later
demands: Arrest of Shahjahan Sheikh and aides; return of grabbed land; justice for sexual-assault complaints
state_response: Prohibitory orders; NHRC team visited; Governor sought immediate arrest; Calcutta HC ordered CBI probe (SC upheld)
outcome: Shahjahan Sheikh arrested 29 Feb 2024 after 55 days and suspended by TMC; protester Rekha Patra became BJP Lok Sabha candidate
election_within_6_months: yes: Lok Sabha 2024-04-19 to 2024-06-01 (results 2024-06-04); Andhra Pradesh 2024-05-13; Odisha May-June 2024

name: Haldwani (Banbhoolpura) violence over madrasa-mosque demolition
trigger: Court-ordered demolition of an unauthorised madrasa and mosque in Muslim-majority Banbhoolpura
organisers: Local residents (spontaneous)
demands: Halt demolition
internet_shutdown: yes: Haldwani town, restored in most areas by 11 Feb 2024
state_response: Curfew with shoot-at-sight authorisation; 36 arrested; magisterial probe ordered; look-out notices and posters of wanted rioters
outcome: Curfew lifted from outer areas 10 Feb and relaxed in Banbhoolpura after 7 days; ~250 injured
election_within_6_months: yes: Lok Sabha 2024-04-19 to 2024-06-01 (results 2024-06-04); Andhra Pradesh 2024-05-13; Odisha May-June 2024

name: Farmers' 'Delhi Chalo 2.0': Shambhu and Khanauri border confrontation

organisers: Samyukt Kisan Morcha (Non-Political) and Kisan Mazdoor Morcha (Jagjit Singh Dallewal, Sarwan Singh Pandher)
demands: Legal MSP guarantee for all crops per Swaminathan formula; debt waiver; withdrawal of cases; pensions
deaths: 6 by ~day 20 incl. Shubhkaran Singh, 21, killed by gunshot at Khanauri on 21 Feb 2024 (Tribune); 5 deaths 16-23 Feb, three by cardiac arrest (Outlook)
internet_shutdown: yes: Haryana suspended mobile internet in Ambala and other border districts (widely reported; not detailed in cited URLs)
state_response: Haryana police multi-layer barricades, tear gas, rubber bullets; four rounds of talks with Union ministers; Punjab registered murder case in Shubhkaran death
outcome: March halted at borders; sit-in continued for over a year (see Dallewal row); Amnesty condemned use of force; end_date approximates Tribune's '20 days of stir' report
election_within_6_months: yes: Lok Sabha 2024-04-19 to 2024-06-01 (results 2024-06-04); Andhra Pradesh 2024-05-13; Odisha May-June 2024

name: Sonam Wangchuk's 21-day 'climate fast' for Ladakh statehood and Sixth Schedule
trigger: Deadlock in 4-5 March 2024 talks between Leh Apex Body/Kargil Democratic Alliance and MHA
organisers: Sonam Wangchuk; Leh Apex Body (LAB); Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA)
demands: Statehood; Sixth Schedule; Ladakh public service commission; separate Lok Sabha seats for Leh and Kargil
crowd_press: hundreds at launch in sub-zero temperatures; 'thousands' addressed (Outlook)
state_response: No concession; talks remained stalled
outcome: Fast ended 26 Mar 2024; Wangchuk vowed to continue agitation (Delhi march Sept-Oct 2024)
election_within_6_months: yes: Lok Sabha 2024-04-19 to 2024-06-01 (results 2024-06-04); Andhra Pradesh 2024-05-13; Odisha May-June 2024

name: NEET-UG 2024 paper-leak protests
trigger: Results on 4 June 2024 with 67 perfect scores, grace marks, and Patna/Hazaribagh paper-leak evidence

demands: Re-examination; CBI/SC-monitored probe; scrapping of NTA; resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan
state_response: CBI probe ordered; grace marks withdrawn for 1,563 candidates with re-test on 23 June; Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act 2024 notified; students who protested faced notices (later withdrawn before SC)

trigger: Education Ministry cancelled 18 June UGC-NET for 9 lakh candidates on 19 June after I4C input that integrity 'may be compromised'

outcome: Exam rescheduled; NTA restructuring committee announced (Radhakrishnan panel)
election_within_6_months: yes: Lok Sabha 2024-04-19 to 2024-06-01 (results 2024-06-04); Andhra Pradesh 2024-05-13; Odisha May-June 2024; J&K 2024-09-18 to 2024-10-01; Haryana 2024-10-05; Jharkhand 2024-11-13/20; Maharashtra 2024-11-20

name: Hathras satsang stampede aftermath (victims' families and opposition protests)
trigger: Crowd crush at Bhole Baba (Suraj Pal) satsang on 2 July 2024 killing 121; ~2.5 lakh attended against permission for 80,000

demands: Accountability of preacher and organisers; compensation and jobs for kin; judicial probe
state_response: UP govt ordered judicial commission and SIT; FIR against organisers (not the preacher) for hiding evidence; compensation announced
outcome: Judicial commission exonerated Bhole Baba and blamed organisers and local administration; families protested the findings; end_date = month-end (protests sporadic)

outcome: Accused sent to judicial custody; HC bail later; Delhi coaching-regulation push

name: RG Kar rape-murder protests: junior doctors' strike and 'Reclaim the Night'
city_or_district: Kolkata (RG Kar Medical College, Esplanade, Swasthya Bhawan)
trigger: Rape and murder of a postgraduate trainee doctor at R.G. Kar Medical College on 9 Aug 2024
organisers: West Bengal Junior Doctors' Front; 'Reclaim the Night' citizens' collective (Rimjhim Sinha); IMA; residents' associations
demands: Justice and CBI probe; removal of principal and police officials; hospital safety; later CM's health secretary's removal
crowd_press: n/a (marches in 40+ Kolkata neighbourhoods on 14 Aug; 'thousands' on 4 Sept)
state_response: Probe transferred to CBI by Calcutta HC; SC took suo motu cognisance; state talks with doctors; police lathicharge at Nabanna march (see separate row)
outcome: Junior doctors' fast ended 21 Oct 2024 after meeting CM (widely reported; end_date from that); Sanjay Roy convicted Jan 2025; cited URLs cover Aug-Sept phases

name: Badlapur school sexual-abuse protest and rail blockade
trigger: Sexual abuse of two kindergarten girls by a school attendant; perceived delay by school and police
organisers: Parents and local residents (spontaneous); MNS/others joined
demands: Arrest and swift prosecution; action against school management and police
crowd_press: 'hundreds' on tracks (Deccan Herald)

outcome: Bombay HC took suo motu cognisance; accused Akshay Shinde later killed in police encounter (Sept 2024; widely reported)

name: Bharat Bandh against Supreme Court SC/ST sub-classification ruling
state: Nationwide (Bihar, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh most affected)
trigger: Supreme Court 1 Aug 2024 ruling permitting sub-classification within SC/ST quotas and discussing creamy layer
organisers: Reservation Bachao Sangharsh Samiti; Dalit and Adivasi organisations; supported by BSP and some opposition parties
demands: Reverse/legislate against sub-classification; no creamy layer for SC/ST
state_response: Rail-track protests at Sitamarhi, Purnea, Muzaffarpur; clashes with police in Bihar; 'no major impact' in Haryana (AIR)
outcome: Mixed response; Union Cabinet had earlier stated no creamy layer for SC/ST (widely reported)

name: Nabanna Abhijan march and BJP bandh over RG Kar case
trigger: RG Kar rape-murder; call by 'Paschim Banga Chhatra Samaj' to march on state secretariat
organisers: Paschim Banga Chhatra Samaj (student group); BJP called 12-hour Bengal bandh on 28 Aug
demands: Resignation of CM Mamata Banerjee; justice in RG Kar case
state_response: Barricades, lathicharge, tear gas, water cannon; many detained; police injured
outcome: March dispersed; BJP bandh next day; political polarisation ahead of 2026 polls

name: Ladakh 'Delhi Chalo' padyatra and Wangchuk's Delhi fast
city_or_district: Leh to New Delhi (Singhu border, Ladakh Bhawan)
trigger: Stalled MHA talks on Ladakh statehood and Sixth Schedule
organisers: Sonam Wangchuk with ~100-150 Ladakhi marchers; LAB and KDA
demands: Statehood; Sixth Schedule; Ladakh PSC and job reservation; two Lok Sabha seats
crowd_press: 'over 100 activists' on the march (Greater Kashmir)
