outcome: Fast at Ladakh Bhawan ended 21 Oct 2024 after MHA assurance of talks (widely reported; end_date from that); talks resumed Dec 2024-Jan 2025

name: Rajasthan SI recruitment 2021 paper-leak protests (for and against cancellation)
trigger: RPSC 2021 sub-inspector exam paper leaked and sold for Rs 15-20 lakh; 50 trainee SIs arrested; SIT recommended cancellation
organisers: Unemployed youth (incl. two who sat atop a water tank from 10 Nov 2024); Rashtriya Loktantrik Party (Hanuman Beniwal) protest 26 Apr 2025; selected candidates' families protested against cancellation
demands: Cancel the exam and re-conduct (aspirants/RLP) vs. protect innocent selected candidates (families)
state_response: Bhajanlal Sharma govt delayed decision; matter in Rajasthan High Court
outcome: Rajasthan HC cancelled the SI Recruitment Exam 2021 (2025); start_date = water-tank protest; end_date = RLP agitation

name: Manipur: Jiribam killings protests and attacks on ministers' homes
city_or_district: Imphal East/West, Bishnupur, Thoubal, Kakching; Jiribam
trigger: Recovery of bodies of six Meitei women and children abducted in Jiribam on 11 Nov 2024 after a gunfight
organisers: Meitei civil groups and Meira Paibis (largely spontaneous mobs)
demands: Action against Kuki militants; removal of AFSPA re-imposition; action against CM; resignation of MLAs
deaths: n/a (protest deaths not reported in cited sources)
internet_shutdown: yes: mobile internet suspended in seven districts (Imphal West/East, Bishnupur, Thoubal, Kakching, Kangpokpi, Churachandpur) from 16 Nov 2024, then extended
state_response: Indefinite curfew in Imphal valley; houses of 13 ministers/MLAs incl. CM's son-in-law vandalised or torched; attempt on CM's residence repelled; AFSPA re-imposed in six police-station areas (rallies against it)
outcome: Coalition strain; CM N. Biren Singh resigned 9 Feb 2025 and President's Rule imposed 13 Feb 2025 (see Kangpokpi row)

name: Sambhal Shahi Jama Masjid survey violence
trigger: Second court-ordered survey of the Shahi Jama Masjid (claimed to be built over a Harihar temple) on 24 Nov 2024
organisers: Local Muslim residents (spontaneous crowd); mosque committee accused by police
demands: Halt the survey
state_response: Outsiders barred; FIRs against SP MP Zia-ur-Rehman Barq and MLA's son; 70+ arrests; SIT chargesheets 159 accused; mosque committee chief Zafar Ali arrested; judicial commission (2026) called it 'pre-planned conspiracy'
outcome: ~20 security personnel injured; recurrent mosque-temple disputes; political controversy

name: Farmers' protest phase 2: Dallewal's 131-day fast and clearance of Shambhu/Khanauri
trigger: No legal MSP guarantee after a year of border sit-ins; Dallewal began fast unto death 26 Nov 2024
organisers: SKM (Non-Political) led by Jagjit Singh Dallewal; Kisan Mazdoor Morcha (Sarwan Singh Pandher)
demands: Legal MSP guarantee; debt waiver; implementation of 2021 assurances
violence: none (fast phase); Punjab Police forcibly cleared camps 19 Mar 2025
state_response: Supreme Court-appointed high-powered committee; SC monitored Dallewal's health; Centre opened talks Jan-Feb 2025; Punjab Police detained Dallewal and Pandher and razed both camps on 19 Mar 2025; Punjab told SC highways cleared 28 Mar 2025
outcome: Dallewal ended fast 6 Apr 2025 after 131 days; Centre-farmers meeting fixed for 4 May 2025; year-long blockade ended

name: BPSC 70th CCE paper-leak protests, Patna
trigger: Alleged leak and irregularities in 13 Dec 2024 BPSC 70th prelims (Bapu exam centre chaos; normalisation row)
organisers: Aspirants; coaching teachers Khan Sir and Guru Rahman; Prashant Kishor (Jan Suraaj); MP Pappu Yadav's supporters

outcome: BPSC refused blanket re-exam (re-test only for one centre); Kishor ended fast; issue carried into Bihar 2025 campaign
election_within_6_months: yes: Delhi assembly 2025-02-05; Bihar assembly Nov 2025 (~10 months later)

name: Kerala ASHA workers' 265-day sit-in outside the Secretariat
trigger: Low honorarium and no retirement benefit for Accredited Social Health Activists; delayed payments
organisers: Kerala ASHA Health Workers Association (KAHWA); later supported by opposition and some unions
demands: Monthly honorarium of Rs 21,000; Rs 5 lakh retirement benefit; timely payment
crowd_press: n/a (sit-in by hundreds of ASHAs; Secretariat blockade 17 Mar 2025)

outcome: Strike concluded 1 Nov 2025 (Kerala Formation Day) after 265 days with core demands unmet; agitation shifted to district level; start_date back-calculated from 265 days
election_within_6_months: yes: Delhi assembly 2025-02-05 (prior); Bihar assembly 2025-11-06/11 (results 2025-11-14); Kerala assembly April 2026 (~5 months after end)

name: Tamil Nadu and southern states' 'fair delimitation' mobilisation (JAC meeting) and BJP counter-protests
state: Tamil Nadu; Karnataka; Kerala; Telangana; Punjab
trigger: Fear that post-census delimitation would cut southern states' Lok Sabha seats; CM Stalin convened all-party meet 5 Mar and Joint Action Committee 22 Mar 2025
organisers: DMK govt / CM M.K. Stalin; southern CMs and parties; Karnataka DyCM D.K. Shivakumar represented Karnataka; TN BJP (black-flag protests)

name: Manipur Kuki-Zo protests against 'free movement' directive (Kangpokpi)
trigger: Union Home Minister Amit Shah's order for free movement on all Manipur roads from 8 Mar 2025 under President's Rule; Meitei FOCS 'peace march' toward Kangpokpi
organisers: Kuki-Zo Council, Committee on Tribal Unity (COTU) and local Kuki groups
demands: No free movement until separate administration; oppose Meitei entry into hills
state_response: Security forces fired on protesters blocking NH-2; state bus escorted; Kuki-Zo groups called indefinite shutdown in hill districts
outcome: First death under President's Rule (imposed 13 Feb 2025 after CM Biren Singh's resignation); highways remained contested

name: West Bengal dismissed school teachers' protests after Supreme Court annulled 25,753 SSC jobs
city_or_district: Kolkata (Kasba DI office, SSC Bhavan Salt Lake, Shahid Minar); district DI offices
trigger: Supreme Court on 3 Apr 2025 upheld cancellation of 25,753 teaching and non-teaching appointments from the 'tainted' 2016 SSC recruitment
organisers: Jogyo Shikshak Shikshika Adhikar Mancha ('eligible teachers' forum) and other dismissed-teacher groups; left unions and BJP backed protests
demands: Publish list separating 'tainted' from 'untainted' candidates; restore jobs of untainted teachers; accountability of state and SSC
crowd_press: 'thousands' at Salt Lake sit-in (The Wire)
state_response: Police lathicharge at Kasba DI office on 8 Apr 2025 after protesters broke lock; several injured, arrests; state sought SC review; interim permission for untainted teachers to work till Dec 2025 (widely reported)
outcome: Relay hunger strike and sit-in at Shahid Minar continued for months; issue became a 2026 election plank; end_date = end of first month (sit-in ongoing)

name: Murshidabad anti-Waqf (Amendment) Act violence
trigger: Protests against the Waqf (Amendment) Act 2025 turned into rioting, arson and looting; father and son killed by mob in Samserganj
organisers: Local Muslim groups and spontaneous crowds; opposition BJP later mobilised Hindu victims
demands: Repeal of Waqf (Amendment) Act 2025
internet_shutdown: yes: parts of Murshidabad, Malda and Birbhum
state_response: 300+ arrested; Calcutta HC ordered central forces (BSF) deployment; route marches by BSF, RAF and state police; CM Mamata Banerjee said Act would not be implemented in Bengal
outcome: Hundreds displaced to Malda; set the stage for a polarised 2026 Bengal election (Deccan Herald)
election_within_6_months: yes: Delhi assembly 2025-02-05 (prior); Bihar Nov 2025 (~7 months later)

name: Pahalgam attack aftermath: nationwide candle marches, Kashmir bandh and backlash against Kashmiris
city_or_district: Srinagar, Pahalgam, Patna, Chandigarh, Delhi and others
trigger: Killing of 26 tourists at Baisaran, Pahalgam on 22 Apr 2025
organisers: All-party groups in J&K (NC, PDP etc.); Mahagathbandhan in Patna; students; traders' bandh in Kashmir
demands: Action against Pakistan-based terrorists; solidarity with victims; protection of Kashmiri students
violence: none (marches); harassment and evictions of Kashmiri students reported in several states (Al Jazeera)
state_response: All-party meeting in Srinagar endorsed Centre's steps against Pakistan; Operation Sindoor on 7 May 2025
outcome: Rare Kashmir-wide bandh against terrorism; Kashmiri students sought protection; followed by Operation Sindoor

name: Anti-Pakistan / pro-Operation Sindoor 'Tiranga Yatra' rallies
city_or_district: Delhi, Dehradun, Srinagar, Anantnag, Katra, Mumbai, Patna, Chennai and others
trigger: Operation Sindoor strikes on 7 May 2025 after the Pahalgam attack; ceasefire 10 May
organisers: BJP (11-day nationwide outreach), state governments, ex-servicemen groups
demands: Celebrate armed forces; support government's Pakistan policy (pro-government rallies rather than protest)
state_response: Government-backed; CMs and Union ministers led processions
outcome: Mass mobilisation; Opposition held separate all-party demands for special session (not covered in cited URLs)

name: Kolkata (Kasba) law-college gang-rape protests
trigger: Gang-rape of a 24-year-old law student on campus on 25 June 2025; prime accused Monojit Mishra identified as a TMC-linked student leader
organisers: Students, 'Reclaim the Night' activists, SFI/left groups; BJP and ABVP (separate protests and 'fact-finding' visit); Bengal LoP Suvendu Adhikari
demands: Fast-track trial; action against TMC-linked accused and college authorities; women's safety on campuses
state_response: Four arrested incl. security guard; five-member SIT; NCW suo motu cognisance; BJP supporters assaulted Reclaim the Night protesters at the college on 30 June (The Wire)
outcome: BJP held Kasba-wide protest 2 July 2025; case fed into 2026 election campaign on women's safety

name: Maharashtra anti-'Hindi imposition' mobilisation and Thackeray cousins' joint rally
trigger: Government Resolutions making Hindi the default third language in Marathi/English-medium primary schools (Classes 1-5) under the three-language formula
organisers: MNS (Raj Thackeray) and Shiv Sena (UBT) (Uddhav Thackeray); Marathi literary and teachers' groups (earlier small protests, incl. a case against a university professor for an 'illegal' protest)
demands: Withdraw the GRs; no compulsory Hindi in primary classes; protect Marathi
state_response: Fadnavis govt withdrew both GRs on 29 June 2025 and set up a committee (Narendra Jadhav) on language policy, pre-empting the planned 5 July morcha
outcome: Planned protest converted into a 'victory' rally on 5 July 2025 where the Thackeray cousins shared a stage after ~20 years; GRs withdrawn

name: Central trade unions' general strike (Bharat Bandh) of 9 July 2025
state: Nationwide (Kerala, West Bengal, Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar most affected)
trigger: Four labour codes, privatisation, contractualisation, 17-point charter ignored
organisers: Joint platform of 10 central trade unions (INTUC, AITUC, CITU, HMS, SEWA, AIUTUC, AICCTU, TUCC, LPF, UTUC) with SKM support
demands: Withdraw labour codes; stop privatisation; MSP; minimum wage; fill vacancies
crowd_press: 'varying impact across states' (Deccan Herald)
state_response: No concession; services largely unaffected in many states (Tribune)
outcome: Symbolic; followed by 12 Feb 2026 strike

name: Goalpara (Paikan Reserve Forest) eviction protest and police firing
trigger: Eviction of ~1,080 mostly Bengali-speaking Muslim families from 140 ha of Paikan Reserve Forest; administration began digging up the access road on 17 July 2025
organisers: Evicted residents (spontaneous)
demands: Stop demolitions and road-cutting; rehabilitation
deaths: 1 (19-year-old, named variously as Sakuar Ali / Shakuar Hussain); several injured
state_response: Police fired on crowd (claimed self-defence); protesters arrested; The Wire reported medical neglect of the injured; CM blamed 'encroachers'
outcome: Eviction completed; drives continued across Assam into the 2026 election

name: Bihar 'Voter Adhikar Yatra' against Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls
city_or_district: Sasaram (Rohtas) to Patna via 23 districts (Muzaffarpur, Hisua etc.)
trigger: ECI's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) dropped ~65 lakh names from draft rolls ahead of Bihar polls; Congress 'vote chori' campaign
organisers: Rahul Gandhi (Congress) with Tejashwi Yadav (RJD) and INDIA bloc partners
demands: Stop/undo SIR deletions; restore excluded voters (migrants, Dalits, poor); ECI accountability
crowd_press: n/a (16-day, 1,300+ km yatra across 50 constituencies; roadshows)
violence: none (BJP workers protested the yatra in Hisua)
state_response: ECI dismissed allegations as 'politically motivated' (17 Aug 2025); BJP counter-protests
outcome: Concluded at Gandhi Maidan, Patna on 1 Sept 2025; NDA nonetheless won Bihar in Nov 2025

name: Maratha quota: Jarange's Azad Maidan hunger strike, Mumbai
trigger: Non-implementation of Kunbi-certificate ('sage-soyare') demand; Jarange marched from Jalna to Mumbai
organisers: Manoj Jarange-Patil; Maratha Kranti Morcha
demands: OBC reservation for Marathas via Kunbi status; Hyderabad gazetteer as proof; notification of 'sage-soyare'
crowd_organiser: '3 crore Marathas will participate' (Jarange's advance claim, Deccan Herald)
crowd_press: n/a (no verified figure; press described supporters blocking CSMT roads and camping in heritage zone)
state_response: Mumbai Police granted conditional permission; 10-member ministerial committee under Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil; Bombay HC directed clearing of roads (widely reported)
outcome: Fast ended 2 Sept 2025 after govt GR accepting Hyderabad gazetteer for Kunbi certificates (widely reported; end_date from that); cited URLs cover 29-31 Aug

name: 'I Love Muhammad' poster row protests across Uttar Pradesh
city_or_district: Kanpur (Rawatpur); Unnao, Kaushambi, Lucknow, Bareilly and others
trigger: Dispute over 'I Love Muhammad' boards during Mawlid procession in Kanpur on 4 Sept 2025; FIR on 9 Sept against 9 named and 15 unidentified persons
organisers: Local Muslim groups; Ittehad-e-Millat Council (Tauqeer Raza Khan) called 26 Sept protest
demands: Withdraw FIRs; right to display the slogan; action against Hindu groups who objected
state_response: Multiple FIRs and arrests across UP districts; permission for 26 Sept Bareilly protest refused (see Bareilly row)
outcome: Spread to several states; culminated in Bareilly violence of 26 Sept 2025

name: Ladakh statehood agitation: 35-day hunger strike and Leh violence of 24 Sept 2025
city_or_district: Leh (NDS Memorial Park, BJP office, Hill Council)
trigger: Hunger strike by Wangchuk and 15 others from 10 Sept; two hunger strikers hospitalised 23 Sept; LAB youth wing called shutdown and protest 24 Sept
organisers: Leh Apex Body (incl. youth wing) and Sonam Wangchuk; Kargil Democratic Alliance supported
demands: Statehood; Sixth Schedule; Ladakh PSC; two Lok Sabha seats; early resumption of MHA talks
crowd_press: n/a (thousands of mostly young protesters; no figure published)
internet_shutdown: yes: Leh (mobile internet curbs alongside curfew; widely reported, not detailed in cited URLs)
state_response: Tear gas, lathicharge, police firing; BJP office and police vehicles torched; curfew in Leh for days; Section 163 orders; Wangchuk detained under NSA on 26 Sept (see next row); MHA ordered judicial probe by Justice (retd) B.S. Chauhan; MHA-LAB/KDA talks held 6 Oct 2025
outcome: Deadliest day of the Ladakh movement; talks resumed under shadow of detentions; anniversary shutdown in 2026
foreign_funding_or_amplification_claims: Ladakh administration/LG blamed Wangchuk's 'provocative speeches' referencing the Nepal Gen-Z agitation and Arab Spring; officials hinted at a 'foreign hand', which the Leh Apex Body rejected while demanding a judicial probe (Deccan Herald). No court finding of foreign funding found; FCRA action against Wangchuk's SECMOL/HIAL was reported separately (not in cited URLs)

name: Manipur: boycotts and clashes around PM Modi's first post-conflict visit
trigger: PM Modi's 13 Sept 2025 visit (first since May 2023) to Churachandpur and Imphal; vandalism of PM cutouts and detentions
organisers: CORCOM (valley insurgent conglomerate) and COCOMI boycott; Kuki-Zo youth groups; Hmar/Vaiphei groups refused to perform
demands: Separate administration (Kuki-Zo); territorial integrity and action on 'illegal immigrants' (Meitei groups); accountability for 2023 violence
state_response: Rs 7,300 crore projects announced; two youths detained for vandalising cutouts; mob clashed with security forces 14 Sept; Kuki leader's house torched
outcome: Visit left 'disappointment' (Quint); conflict unresolved into 2026

name: Kurmi indefinite rail-roko for ST status (2025 round)
city_or_district: Muri, Rai, Tatisilwai (Ranchi); Barkakana; Parasnath; Charhi; Pradhankhanta (Dhanbad); Galudih; Chandrapura
trigger: Renewed indefinite rail and road blockade from 20 Sept 2025 for ST status and Kurmali recognition
organisers: Adivasi Kurmi Samaj (AKS) and allied Kurmi organisations in Jharkhand, Bengal, Odisha
demands: ST status for Kurmis; Kurmali language in Eighth Schedule
crowd_press: n/a ('thousands of passengers stranded'; protesters squatted on tracks at 9+ stations)
state_response: Railways cancelled, diverted or short-terminated 100+ trains on day one (25 cancelled/24 diverted in Dhanbad division; 12 cancelled incl. Vande Bharat and Rajdhani/11 diverted in Ranchi division); police deployed
outcome: Blockade disrupted services for at least two days; demand unmet; end_date approximate

name: Bareilly violence after Friday prayers ('I Love Muhammad' row)
trigger: Crowd gathered after Friday prayers on 26 Sept 2025 answering Ittehad-e-Millat Council call despite denied permission; stone-pelting at police
organisers: Ittehad-e-Millat Council chief Maulana Tauqeer Raza Khan and aides
demands: Action against those who removed 'I Love Muhammad' posters; withdraw FIRs
crowd_press: 'huge crowd' (Wikipedia/India TV); no figure
state_response: Lathicharge; police personnel injured; Tauqeer Raza and 7 co-accused arrested; FIRs against ~1,700 unidentified persons at four stations; govt considered NSA; CM Yogi Adityanath warned 'no one can hold system hostage'
outcome: Dozens detained; aide detained for mobilising crowd; heavy security for subsequent Fridays

name: Ladakh: curfew, Wangchuk's NSA detention and campaign for his release
trigger: Detention of Sonam Wangchuk under National Security Act on 26 Sept 2025 by Leh DM, transfer to Jodhpur Central Jail
organisers: Leh Apex Body, Kargil Democratic Alliance; Wangchuk's wife Gitanjali Angmo (SC petition); opposition parties
demands: Release of Wangchuk; judicial probe into firing; resumption of talks
state_response: Curfew in Leh continued at least four days after detention; Supreme Court sought Centre/Ladakh response (Oct 2025); PIB statement on commitment to dialogue; MHA revoked detention 14 Mar 2026
outcome: Wangchuk released from Jodhpur jail on 14 Mar 2026 after ~170 days; he later led 2026 Jantar Mantar hunger strike and Leh anniversary padyatra
election_within_6_months: yes: Bihar assembly 2025-11-06/11 (results 2025-11-14); Assam 2026-04-09, Tamil Nadu 2026-04-23, Kerala/West Bengal/Puducherry April 2026 (all results 2026-05-04)
foreign_funding_or_amplification_claims: Administration cited Wangchuk's references to Nepal and Arab Spring as provocation (see previous row); no court finding of foreign funding found in sources

name: West Bengal TMC protests against SIR of electoral rolls (pre-2026 poll)
city_or_district: Kolkata (Maidan to Jorasanko); Thakurnagar/Chandpara (Matua belt); Krishnanagar
trigger: Launch of SIR in Bengal on 4 Nov 2025; deaths of booth-level officers (4 BLO deaths by late Nov incl. Rinku Tarafdar's suicide) and reported suicides of anxious residents
organisers: Trinamool Congress led by CM Mamata Banerjee and Abhishek Banerjee
demands: Halt 'coercive' SIR ('Silent Invisible Rigging'); protect refugee-belt and minority voters; accountability of ECI for BLO deaths
crowd_press: n/a ('mega rally' 4 Nov; 3-km march 25 Nov)
deaths: 0 (protest); TMC claimed 35 SIR-linked deaths; 4 BLO deaths reported
state_response: ECI told TMC not to interfere with BLOs; BJP accused TMC of shielding infiltrators
outcome: SIR enumeration concluded 4 Dec 2025; roll revision became central battleground of the April 2026 election
election_within_6_months: yes: West Bengal assembly April 2026 (results 2026-05-04); Bihar 2025-11-06/11 (concurrent)

name: Delhi India Gate air-pollution protests and detentions
trigger: AQI above 350 ('very poor') for weeks; parents, students and environmental groups demanded emergency action
organisers: Parents' groups, students (JNUSU, AISA-DU), environmental collectives; later Students for Society and others
demands: Right to clean air; enforcement against stubble burning, vehicles and construction; health emergency measures
crowd_press: 'hundreds' (Al Jazeera/Down To Earth)
state_response: ~80 detained on 9 Nov for violating prohibitory orders (India Gate 'not a protest site'); JNUSU president and others reportedly taken to undisclosed location; on 23 Nov police alleged pepper spray by protesters, arrested 15-22, six sent to 3-day custody; Index on Censorship criticised suppression
outcome: No policy concession; police claimed links of some accused to a 'radical group' after pro-Maoist (Madvi Hidma) slogans, which SFS disowned
election_within_6_months: yes: Bihar assembly 2025-11-06/11 (results 2025-11-14); Assam 2026-04-09, Tamil Nadu 2026-04-23, Kerala/West Bengal/Puducherry April 2026 (all results 2026-05-04)
foreign_funding_or_amplification_claims: Delhi Police claimed six accused were linked to a 'radical' group after slogans backing slain Maoist leader Madvi Hidma (Deccan Herald); SFS distanced itself; no foreign-funding or bot claim found

name: Farmers' nationwide protests against India-US interim trade framework
state: Nationwide (Punjab, Haryana, UP, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu)
trigger: India-US interim trade framework announced Feb 2026; fears of subsidised US farm, dairy and GM imports
organisers: Samyukt Kisan Morcha (100+ unions) with central trade unions
demands: Scrap/renegotiate the deal; exclude agriculture and dairy; consult farmers
crowd_press: 'thousands' nationwide (Reuters via Kuwait Times/Tribune PK); copies of pact burned in fields
state_response: Convoys stopped near Delhi; Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said dairy, poultry, rice, wheat and most farm goods excluded; PIB/AIR 'debunked' viral claims of harm to farmers
outcome: Deal defended by govt; SKM later held Delhi protest against FTAs on 21 July 2026 (not separately sourced); dates = month only (exact start not given in sources)
election_within_6_months: yes: Assam 2026-04-09, Tamil Nadu 2026-04-23, Kerala/West Bengal/Puducherry April 2026 (all results 2026-05-04)
foreign_funding_or_amplification_claims: Government fact-check unit called claims that the deal harms farmers 'viral misinformation' (AIR); no foreign-funding allegation found

name: All-India general strike (Bharat Bandh) of 12 February 2026
trigger: Implementation of four labour codes; Draft Seed Bill, Electricity Amendment Bill, SHANTI nuclear Act; India-US trade deal
organisers: Joint Platform of Central Trade Unions (CITU, AITUC, INTUC, HMS, AICCTU, LPF, UTUC etc.) and sectoral federations; SKM support
demands: Withdraw labour codes and listed bills; MSP; stop privatisation
crowd_organiser: 'more than 30 crore workers could take part' (union estimate)
crowd_press: n/a (disruption to govt offices, banks, transport reported)
state_response: No concession; essential services maintained
outcome: Symbolic nationwide shutdown weeks before state polls
election_within_6_months: yes: Assam 2026-04-09, Tamil Nadu 2026-04-23, Kerala/West Bengal/Puducherry April 2026 (all results 2026-05-04)

name: Assam pre-election eviction drives and displaced families' protests (Andherijuli, Dhekiajuli, Dhubri)
city_or_district: Andherijuli (Azara circle, Kamrup, near Guwahati airport); Dhekiajuli (Sonitpur); Dhubri
trigger: 27 Feb 2026 notices giving families unable to prove eligibility 15 days to vacate ~700 bighas at Andherijuli; ~300 families displaced, tarpaulin shelters and camps also demolished (on eve of Eid); wider drives (e.g., 1,400 Bengali-origin Muslim families in Dhubri) ahead of 9 Apr 2026 polls
organisers: Displaced (largely Bengali-origin and indigenous Muslim) families; All Assam Minority Students' Union (AAMSU) sit-in at Dhekiajuli over eviction and rehabilitation; Congress/AIUDF raised the issue
demands: Halt evictions; rehabilitation and compensation; land rights
crowd_press: n/a (~300 families displaced at Andherijuli; 'hundreds of families' per Outlook)
state_response: CM Himanta Biswa Sarma defended evictions as a strategy against 'undocumented migrants'; Supreme Court petitions on Assam evictions pending (The Wire)
outcome: BJP-led NDA won 102/126 seats on 4 May 2026; evictions continued post-poll; start_date = end of 15-day notice period (approximate)

name: Opposition protests against LPG and fuel price hikes amid Iran war / Hormuz disruption
city_or_district: Hyderabad, Karimnagar, Mumbai (Ghatkopar), Kohima and others
trigger: US-Israel campaign against Iran from 28 Feb 2026 and Iranian closure of the Strait of Hormuz pushed the Indian crude basket to ~USD 113/bbl by 11 Mar; Centre cut excise by Rs 10/litre on 26-27 Mar 2026 but raised domestic LPG by Rs 29/cylinder (second hike in three months) and petrol/diesel by Rs 3/litre on 15 May 2026, the first retail hike in ~four years, days after state election results
organisers: Congress and Youth Congress units; other opposition parties
demands: Roll back LPG/fuel hikes; relief for households
state_response: PM Modi urged voluntary austerity, calling fuel saving 'patriotism'; no rollback
outcome: Rolling, localised Congress protests through spring 2026 (Hyderabad 25 Mar, Kohima 30 May, Mumbai 1 Jun, Karimnagar 8 Jun); Congress said govt was 'recovering political costs' after polls; NO nationwide Bharat bandh over the Iran war/Hormuz/fuel found in searches
election_within_6_months: yes: Assam 2026-04-09, Tamil Nadu 2026-04-23, Kerala/West Bengal/Puducherry April 2026 (all results 2026-05-04)

name: Manipur: Tronglaobi bombing protests and shootings (Moirang/Bishnupur)
trigger: Bomb hurled at a house at 1 am on 7 Apr 2026 killing a 5-year-old boy and 6-month-old girl; mob stormed nearby central-force camp
organisers: Local Meitei residents and women's groups (spontaneous); torch rallies
demands: Arrest of perpetrators; removal of central-force camp; justice for children
deaths: 2 protesters shot dead at camp (WION); at least 7 killed in total since 7 Apr incl. the two children (Al Jazeera, 22 Apr 2026)
state_response: Security forces fired on mob attacking camp; more than a dozen arrested; police clashed with torch-rally protesters (Business Standard, 21 Apr); initial probe pointed to 'local elements'
outcome: Renewed cycle of violence in third year of conflict; fed into NRC/census agitation later in 2026
election_within_6_months: yes: Assam 2026-04-09, Tamil Nadu 2026-04-23, Kerala/West Bengal/Puducherry April 2026 (all results 2026-05-04)

name: Noida garment and factory workers' wage protest (Phase 2 Hosiery Complex)
trigger: Haryana raised minimum wages while UP did not; wages of Rs 9,000-13,000 vs. rising living costs amid the Iran-war price spike; strike began 10 Apr 2026 at Phase 2 Hosiery Complex and spread to Motherson, Richa Global, Sahu Exports and other plants
organisers: Largely unorganised garment and auto-component workers; AICCTU and other left unions later demanded releases
demands: Minimum wage of Rs 20,000-26,000/month; overtime pay; parity with Haryana
crowd_press: 'thousands' of garment workers (Al Jazeera, Wikipedia)
state_response: Tear gas and lathicharge on 13 Apr after vehicles torched and stones pelted; ~50 arrested that day and ~300 by 14 Apr (Deccan Herald/Wikipedia); UP govt approved 20-21% interim minimum-wage hike on 18 Apr 2026; a Gurugram court later rejected 'conspiracy' theory against Manesar workers (The Wire)
outcome: Partial win: UP minimum wages raised; hundreds of workers prosecuted; AICCTU protest 17 Apr for releases
election_within_6_months: yes: Assam 2026-04-09, Tamil Nadu 2026-04-23, Kerala/West Bengal/Puducherry April 2026 (all results 2026-05-04)

name: West Bengal post-poll violence and protests after BJP victory
city_or_district: Kolkata (Tollygunge, Kasba), Birbhum, Howrah, Murshidabad, North and South 24 Parganas
trigger: Counting on 4 May 2026 ended 15 years of TMC rule; two persons killed on 5 May; TMC offices attacked; TMC alleged BJP-led violence, BJP denied
organisers: TMC and BJP workers (rival mobilisations); CM Mamata Banerjee contested the result
demands: TMC: protection of workers and probe into violence; BJP: action against TMC 'intimidation'
state_response: CEC Gyanesh Kumar ordered immediate arrests and 'zero tolerance'; CAPF deployed; new BJP govt formation under way
outcome: BJP government formed; end_date approximate (first week after results)

name: Cockroach Janta Party-led Jantar Mantar protests over NEET-UG 2026 leak and exam deaths
trigger: NEET-UG 2026 (3 May) cancelled on 12 May after leak via 'guess papers' (~140 matching questions, Rajasthan); re-test 21 June for 22.79 lakh candidates; more than a dozen aspirants died by suicide before re-exam; CBSE on-screen-marking irregularities
organisers: Cockroach Janta Party (founder Abhijeet Dipke, 30); AISF, AISA, SFI; Cockroach Students' Union of India; Sonam Wangchuk joined with hunger strike (see row)
demands: Resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan; CBI probe and exam-system reform; compensation for families of students who died; withdrawal of cases against protesters
crowd_press: ~20,000 at Monday protests, 'one of the largest anti-government gatherings in years' (Al Jazeera/TIME); >10,000 marched on Parliament 20 July (Al Jazeera)
state_response: Delhi Police leadership changed mid-July; barricades removed and Wangchuk moved to hospital; baton charge and tear gas on 20 July march; Amnesty International criticised crackdown; PM Modi promised action on leaks (24 July)
outcome: Pradhan resigned 25 July 2026 (President accepted; Pralhad Joshi given Education); Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Act 2026 passed; assurances on compensation and withdrawal of cases; CJP called off protests
election_within_6_months: yes: Assam 2026-04-09, Tamil Nadu 2026-04-23, Kerala/West Bengal/Puducherry April 2026 (all results 2026-05-04)
foreign_funding_or_amplification_claims: OFFICIAL: Delhi Police announced on 23 July 2026 that it had identified and blocked 480 Pakistan-based social media handles for 'coordinated misinformation' around the Jantar Mantar protest, saying many had earlier spread anti-India content during Operation Sindoor, and appealed to students to be wary of 'foreign accounts' (Delhi Police on X; India TV; Deccan Herald); in Aug 2026 police alleged a 'digital conspiracy' behind the 20 July violence, issued notices to Meta, Google and X, and probed ~180 influencer/YouTuber accounts and three digital-marketing firms (ETV Bharat; Organiser); police also ordered X to remove posts targeting the PM. PARTISAN: BJYM's Tajinder Bagga circulated a graphic (May 2026) claiming 49% of CJP followers were Pakistani, 14% US, 14% Bangladeshi, 9% Indian, amplified by ABP anchor Chitra Tripathi and OpIndia (which also alleged a Pakistani edited CJP's Wikipedia page). REBUTTALS: Alt News fact-check called the follower claim misleading; founder Dipke posted analytics showing 94% Indian followers (France 24). Pradhan's resignation statement cited 'anti-national forces'. No court or MEA finding on foreign funding found; no evidence that the blocked handles organised or funded the protest was published

name: Sonam Wangchuk's 26-day hunger strike at Jantar Mantar for exam accountability
trigger: NEET-UG 2026 leak and student suicides; Wangchuk joined CJP protest three months after release from NSA detention
organisers: Sonam Wangchuk (with CJP and student groups)
demands: Pradhan's resignation; systemic reform to prevent paper leaks; compensation to bereaved families; no action against protesters
state_response: Mid-July Delhi Police removed barricades and shifted Wangchuk to hospital (organisers said against his will); Rahul Gandhi criticised; doctors warned of organ damage after ~21 lb weight loss; govt gave assurances via talks
outcome: Fast ended 23 July 2026 on assurances of no legal action against protesters, discussion on leak prevention, and compensation; Pradhan resigned two days later
election_within_6_months: yes: Assam 2026-04-09, Tamil Nadu 2026-04-23, Kerala/West Bengal/Puducherry April 2026 (all results 2026-05-04)
foreign_funding_or_amplification_claims: Central Tibetan Administration criticised Wangchuk's comparison of Ladakh with Tibet as 'misplaced, inaccurate' (ThePrint) - a political, not funding, dispute; no foreign-funding claim found in cited sources

name: 20 July 2026 march on Parliament and police crackdown (Cockroach movement)
city_or_district: New Delhi (Jantar Mantar to Parliament Street)
trigger: CJP call to march to Parliament during Monsoon Session after weeks without response to demands
organisers: Cockroach Janta Party; AISA, SFI, AISF; Gen-Z students
demands: Pradhan's resignation; exam reform
crowd_press: >10,000 marchers (Al Jazeera); 'thousands' (NPR)
state_response: Police defied-dispersal orders enforced with tear gas, baton charges and canes; some protesters pelted stones; detentions; Amnesty called it a crackdown on peaceful protest
outcome: CJP founder Dipke announced on 21 July that the movement would not march again 'because the police will hurt the youth again' but would continue the sit-in; Pradhan resigned 25 July
election_within_6_months: yes: Assam 2026-04-09, Tamil Nadu 2026-04-23, Kerala/West Bengal/Puducherry April 2026 (all results 2026-05-04)
foreign_funding_or_amplification_claims: See CJP row (Bagga 'Pakistani followers' claim, Alt News rebuttal); no new official claim found for 20 July specifically

name: Ranchi students' agitation over JPSC/JSSC exam irregularities
city_or_district: Ranchi (Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, Albert Ekka Chowk)
trigger: Alleged irregularities in 14th JPSC prelims results and JSSC exams; viral answer sheet
